GHSA-pxmc-2ffp-8j67: prevent arbitrary certificate revocation via duplicate DB rows

Certificate identity was tracked only by Lemur's internal database row, not
by the actual CA-side certificate. Any authenticated user could upload a
duplicate record for a certificate they didn't own (matching an existing
authority_id and serial) and then revoke it, causing the CA to revoke the
real certificate belonging to another user.

- POST /api/1/certificates/upload now requires AuthorityPermission on the
  specified authority, and rejects uploads whose (authority_id, serial)
  pair already matches an existing certificate (409).
- PUT /api/1/certificates/<id>/revoke now checks authorization and endpoint
  attachment against every certificate row sharing (authority_id, serial)
  with the one being revoked, not just the row named in the request.

Harden combined resource handler against forged resource IDs

Combined resource IDs are unauthenticated deflate+base64 of the resource
list, so a crafted ID could inflate without bound, grow the static cache
without bound, and select arbitrary inner resources at serve time.

- Cap unserializeURLSafe output at 64 KiB.
- Populate the info cache only from the render path (Builder.create); the
  serve path no longer caches reconstructed IDs.
- Serve a reconstructed ID only when every inner resource is a stylesheet
  or script, so a forged ID cannot reference Facelets or dynamic resources.

explanation:
Stop giving product photos a plinth to clash with (#176)

* Per-category delivery explanation on product pages + Discord

Answers the #1 pre-purchase question ('how do I get it?') right on each
product, and mirrors it in Discord.

- src/lib/deliveryInfo.js: bilingual (EN/NL) delivery info per category —
  Robux (Group Payout / Roblox+ method: enable 2FA, 5000 R$/day limit so
  large orders split across days, very large via 2 staff accounts),
  V-Bucks (gift-card code), and a solid code/top-up default.
- ProductDetail: a 'How this is delivered' panel (method + numbered steps +
  good-to-know notes), light-theme styled, with NL labels.
- Discord: /price now shows the delivery method; new /delivery command gives
  the full steps + notes; registered + added to /help.

* admin: one-click suggested sell price from supplier cost

Enter the cost you pay (e.g. on Eldorado/Eneba) and get a 'Suggest price'
button that applies a ~18% markup with a €2 minimum profit, rounded to a
clean .99 — so €140 cost → €165.99, €10 → €11.99. Tune MARKUP/FLOOR in one
place. Existing margin readout stays.

* delivery: drop the Roblox-group join step from Robux (group is only for giveaways)

Robux delivery no longer mentions joining a Roblox group — the group is used
for giveaways, not delivery. Steps are now: enable 2FA → send your username →
we deliver. Updated on the site (EN/NL) and in the Discord bot.

* Forge Coins + Forge Shop, and 'as fast as possible' delivery label

- Forge Coins: a real loyalty currency (append-only ledger, balance = SUM,
  no cached number that can drift). Earn 1 coin per €10 of paid spend,
  awarded once per order (unique index = idempotent on payment retries).
- Forge Shop (account): spend coins on personal discount codes (€5/€10/€25,
  auto-generated single-use coupons) or a giveaway boost. Transactional
  redeem so concurrent spends can't overspend.
- API: GET /account/coins, POST /account/coins/redeem. Nav + route added.
- Migration 012_forge_coins.
- Product page: replaced the 'Estimated delivery ~Xs' line with a simple
  'Delivery: as fast as possible' (NL: 'Levering: zo snel mogelijk').

Verified on real Postgres: earn/idempotency/redeem/overspend all pass; build green.

* Mystery boxes — a real paid 'giveaway' (buy → roll a weighted prize → store credit)

- Migration 013: mystery_box_rewards (weighted prize pool) + mystery_pulls
  (what each buyer won). A mystery box is a product with kind='mystery'.
- mysteryBoxService: weighted roll per unit on payment, pays out as store
  credit via the wallet (tagged = idempotent, no double-pay on retries),
  records the pull + notifies the buyer.
- Hooked into order payment_received.
- Admin: 'Mystery box' toggle + a reward-pool editor (label / odds / € credit)
  in the product modal (GET+PUT /admin/products/:id/mystery).
- Product page: 'What's inside' panel showing every prize + REAL odds.
- Account order page: a celebratory reveal of what you won + credit added.
- Public GET /products/:id/mystery (pool+odds), account GET /orders/:id/mystery.

Verified on real Postgres: roll/credit/record + idempotent re-settle (6/6);
build green. Note: bundles already support any product mix (PS+Xbox, Apex+
Valorant) — create them in Admin → Monetization.

* i18n: Dutch labels for the mystery-box 'What's inside' panel

* Mystery boxes: bulk-luck ('more = better prizes') + a risk-free reroll (1x/box)

- Odds now scale with how many boxes are opened in one order: +8% luck per
  extra box (capped 2x), weighted toward the higher-value prizes — buy more,
  win better. Verified over a large sample (avg prize rises with quantity).
- One reroll per box (migration 014 stamps rerolled_at, claimed atomically so
  it can't be used twice): rolls a fresh prize and the buyer KEEPS the higher
  one — risk-free. POST /account/orders/:id/mystery/:pullId/reroll + a Reroll
  button on the order reveal.

Verified on real Postgres: reroll keeps-the-better + second reroll blocked; build green.

* Drop calendar — scheduled restocks/launches/sales

- Migration 015 + dropService: staff schedule drops (title, category, note,
  date/time); upcoming ones surface on the storefront.
- Public GET /api/drops (upcoming); admin GET/POST/DELETE /api/admin/drops.
- Storefront /drops page (timeline with 'Soon' badges, Discord-alert CTA)
  + a 'Drops' link in the top nav, fully bilingual.
- Admin: a 'Drops' tab in Monetization to schedule/remove drops.
- New drops announce to Discord (best-effort).

Verified on real Postgres (5/5: create/upcoming filter/list/delete); build green.

* Price history chart on product pages

- Migration 016 + price_history: a snapshot on product create and on every
  real price change (dup prices skipped); existing products get a baseline
  point so charts aren't empty.
- Public GET /api/products/:id/price-history.
- Product page: a clean SVG area/line chart with Now + Lowest, and a
  '🔥 lowest price ever' badge when current == lowest. Bilingual labels.

Verified on real Postgres (baseline + change tracking + dedup, 3/3); build green.

* Launch polish: surface engagement features + Discord /drops

Site: a 'Save more & win big' section on the homepage with cards linking to
Forge Coins, Mystery boxes and the Drop calendar — so the new features are
actually discoverable (bilingual).

Discord: new /drops command showing the upcoming drop calendar (live from the
store, with Discord relative timestamps) + a link to the full calendar;
registered and added to /help.

* Live trust stats: refresh instantly on delivery + new review (no fabrication)

The trust stats (delivered count, customers, review count, average rating) are
already computed 100% from real DB rows — nothing seeded or padded (demoSeed
only inserts products; no hardcoded numbers in the UI). This makes them update
INSTANTLY instead of within the 15s cache window: bust the social/stats cache
the moment an order is marked delivered and the moment a review is added, so
the counters and average rating move up right away.

Verified on real Postgres: delivered increments on completion, review count +
rating reflect a real review; boots with no circular-import issue.

* Launch-ready hardening: zero-admin setup, critical fixes, self-running maintenance

Critical fixes:
- productSchema rejected kind='mystery' (enum was digital|physical) → the
  admin's Mystery box toggle could never save. Added 'mystery'.
- Admin fulfillment badge counted status='paid', which doesn't exist →
  always 0. Now counts payment_received/processing/awaiting_fulfillment.

Zero-admin launch:
- Self-scheduling maintenance: piggybacks on live traffic (max 1×/hour per
  instance, non-blocking) so OTP purges, stale-order cleanup and payment
  reminders run WITHOUT CRON_SECRET or Vercel Cron. Launch-check item is
  now ok by default (cron stays as optional backup).
- Starter content on first boot (idempotent, never overwrites admin work):
  the €49.99 Forge Mystery Box with a balanced 5-prize pool (EV ≈ €38.75 →
  ~22% margin, paid as store credit) + an FPS Duo bundle (Apex+Valorant,
  10% off). 'mystery' category gets its own card visual.

Quality:
- Mystery-only orders now AUTO-COMPLETE on payment (the credit payout IS
  the delivery) instead of lingering in the manual queue.
- Forge Shop: redeemed coupon codes persist in the coin history with a
  copy button (a toast was the only place you ever saw the code).

Verified on real Postgres: 5/5 hardening e2e (maintenance fires on traffic,
launch-check ok without CRON_SECRET, mystery auto-complete, fulfillment
query, code-in-history) + 4/4 starter-content e2e + 19/19 regression suite;
build green.

* Discord relay: full automation with ZERO hosting-side Discord secrets + badge fix

The 'Discord automation' launch warning could only be cleared by putting the
bot token / webhook URLs into Vercel. Now the community bot (which already has
the token) pulls the store's events itself:

- Migration 017: discord_outbox queue + a tiny kv table.
- discordService: every sender (order pings, drops, stock alerts, 500 alerts)
  posts directly when a webhook is configured, and otherwise QUEUES the exact
  embed payload in the outbox. Delivery DMs relay the same way (channel 'dm'
  with the buyer's linked Discord id) when no server-side bot token exists.
- POST /api/discord/outbox — HMAC-signed like the digest; returns + marks
  pending events, stamps 'bot seen' in kv, prunes old rows.
- Bot: polls the outbox every 60s and posts events to #leads / #deals (with
  fallbacks) or DMs the buyer. Zero new env vars — reuses REVIEW_INGEST_SECRET.
- Launch check: 'Discord automation' turns OK as soon as the bot has polled in
  the last 24h ('Bot connected via relay'), with a clear hint otherwise.

Also: the admin Support badge now counts only OPEN tickets (action needed), so
resolving a ticket clears the badge — 'pending' means waiting on the customer.

Verified on real Postgres over real HTTP: queue → signed poll → delivered →
second poll empty → bad signature 403 → launch check flips to ok (8/8);
bot load test + build green.

* bot: watchdog retries before paging (cold start / Neon wake is not an outage)

The site watchdog alerted @here after a single failed 15s probe — but a
serverless cold start plus a sleeping Neon database can take 15-25s to wake,
which is a false alarm, not downtime. Verified the API itself is healthy: a
cold boot from a COMPLETELY fresh database (all 17 migrations + seeds) answers
/api/health in ~1.3s, warm in ~12ms. Now the watchdog retries once after 20s
with a 28s timeout and only pages when both probes fail — real outages still
alert within ~1 minute.

* Fix everything reported live + product art + email v3

Fixes from live testing:
- Duplicate €49.99 mystery boxes: the starter seeder raced when Vercel booted
  several instances at once. Now uses a FIXED primary key (insert ON CONFLICT
  DO NOTHING) and heals existing duplicates on boot (keeps the oldest; deletes
  or deactivates extras). Verified with 3 parallel seed calls → exactly 1 box.
- 'Fortnite Accounts' removed from the home sidebar — it was a hardcoded entry
  pointing at the v-bucks category; we don't sell accounts.
- 'Happy customers' now counts people who actually WROTE A REVIEW (stat tile +
  hero avatar row), not everyone who ever ordered — and hides at zero.
- Orders badge vs Fulfillment badge: Orders now shows paid orders awaiting
  delivery; Fulfillment counts exactly the manual queue its page displays.
- Forge Coins grant bug: the order-earn dedupe index blocked a second grant by
  the same admin (same reason+ref) — grants now store ref NULL (attribution is
  in the audit log).

New:
- Write a review on /reviews: verified buyers pick one of their delivered
  orders (new GET /account/reviewable), star + text → posts via the existing
  verified-review endpoint. Guests see how reviews work. Bilingual.
- Admin → Users: 🪙 Coins button to give (or deduct) Forge Coins per user
  (POST /admin/security/users/:id/coins, audited, can't go below 0).
- Product art: per-pack denomination cards (the existing pack SVGs) now win
  over the generic category icon, and syncCatalogImages() backfills them on
  every boot so the LIVE catalog gets its art too.
- Email v3: richer shell for ALL mails (patterned gradient header, badge,
  pill styles) + a redesigned login-code email (lock badge, expiry pill).
  Previous body registered as legacy so deployed DBs auto-upgrade.

Proven on real Postgres (8/8): parallel-seed dedupe, duplicate healing, double
grant, over-deduct block, redeemed code REALLY gives €10 off €25 at checkout,
single-use enforced, reviewable query, queue count. Build green.

* starter: heal duplicate bundles (6x FPS Duo Pack from the pre-fix race)

The old bundle seeder created a random-id bundle per concurrent cold start
before the fixed-id fix shipped, leaving 6 identical 'FPS Duo Pack' rows in
production. Boot now dedupes same-named bundles (keeps the oldest, tiebreak
on id for same-instant rows; bundles have no dependents so DELETE is safe).

Reproduced exactly (6 identical rows, 3 sharing one timestamp) → heals to 1;
parallel re-runs stay at 1 (3/3 on real Postgres).

* Audit round: reroll safety, phone-route crash fix, /balance Discord command

- rerollPull: validate the pull + a non-empty reward pool BEFORE atomically
  claiming the one-time reroll, so an emptied pool can no longer burn the
  buyer's free reroll and crash the request.
- account routes: import badRequest (phone verify routes threw a 500
  ReferenceError on any invalid input instead of a clean 400).
- New signed endpoint POST /api/discord/balance: Forge Coins, store credit
  and loyalty tier for a linked Discord member; the uid is bound into the
  HMAC signature so requests can't be replayed for another member.
- Bot: new /balance command (ephemeral) + /help entry; unlinked members get
  a login pointer.

Verified on real Postgres: 23-check purchase-flow e2e (createOrder ->
payment -> mystery settle -> coins -> auto-complete -> reroll paths),
7-check balance-endpoint HTTP e2e, 19-check regression suite, bot load
test, vite build.

* Add /clearpins staff command to bulk-delete "pinned a message" notices

Every time something is pinned, Discord posts a small "X pinned a message to
this channel" system message. Our setup panels pin on boot, so these pile up.

/clearpins (staff-only) walks the history of every text + announcement channel
and deletes just those pin-notice system messages (MessageType 6) in one go —
normal messages and other system notices are left untouched. Deletes
individually so notices older than 14 days are handled too, paginating up to a
safety cap per channel. Optional `here:true` limits it to the current channel.
Reports how many were removed and calls out any channels it lacked
Manage Messages / Read Message History for.

Verified with a mocked-interaction test: only pin notices deleted across text +
announcement channels, voice channels not scanned, unmanageable channels
skipped and reported; bot load test + lint still green.

* Document REVIEW_INGEST_SECRET in the bot .env.example

The bot needs REVIEW_INGEST_SECRET to poll the signed store relay (order
pings, drops, delivery DMs) and to read /balance and /digest, but it was
missing from the example env file — easy to forget when deploying to a host.
Add it with a note that it must match the value in Vercel, and point the
store URLs at the live domain.

* Fix 5 bugs found in a full site + Discord audit

Frontend
- Checkout page crashed on render: the main component called t() dozens of
  times but never ran useI18n() (only the helper sub-components did), so the
  whole checkout threw a ReferenceError the moment the cart had items. Nobody
  could reach the pay step. Added const { t } = useI18n().

Server
- Gift-card codes were derived purely from Date.now() mod 32, so only 32
  distinct codes could ever be generated — trivially guessable/enumerable
  (drain any outstanding card via the public balance check + redeem) and
  colliding on the UNIQUE index after a few issues. Now generated with
  crypto.randomInt over a 32-char alphabet (~10^24 space); proven 20000/20000
  unique.
- Manual-payment proof confirm/reject never notified the buyer: it checked
  order.user_id, but getOrder() hydrates to camelCase order.userId, so the
  guard was always false. Fixed both call sites; the reject email's order link
  was also an empty string — now points at the public track page.

Discord bot
- Auto-moderation + XP ran inside CLAIMED tickets: claiming renames the
  channel to '✋-ticket-…', which defeated the startsWith('ticket-') check, so
  a customer pasting a trade link in their own claimed ticket got their
  message deleted and publicly warned. Detect tickets by their stable
  'ticket-owner:' topic (survives the rename) via a shared isTicketChannel().
- /suggest could report 'interaction failed' while actually posting: it did
  two Discord round-trips (send + startThread) before its first reply, risking
  the 3s ACK window. Now defers first, then edits the reply.

Verified on real Postgres + mocked-bot: new bugfix e2e (7 checks: proof
confirm/reject notifications, gift-card uniqueness/shape), ticket-exemption
test (scam in a claimed ticket is left alone, public channel still moderated),
gift-card entropy (20000/20000 unique), plus the full suite green — flow-e2e
(23), regression (19), bot load test, and vite build.

* Auto-email gift-card codes to the recipient on issue

Issuing a gift card with a recipient email now delivers the code straight to
that inbox with a new branded 'gift_card' template (code, amount, note, and a
redeem-in-your-wallet call to action) — previously the recipient email was
stored but nothing was ever sent, so staff had to copy the code and send it by
hand. Best-effort: a mail failure never invalidates the (already valid) card;
the API + admin UI report whether it was emailed. Leaving the email blank still
just generates a code to hand out yourself.

The new template auto-rolls out to the live DB via syncEmailTemplates on boot.

Verified on real Postgres: issuing with a recipient logs a gift_card email
whose subject carries the amount and whose rendered code matches the card;
issuing without one sends nothing and the card is still valid (8 checks).

* Add automatic post-delivery review-request email

Every completed order now gets one 'How was your order?' email a day after
delivery, linking straight to the review widget for that order on /track
(works for guest buyers too). Idempotent and self-scheduling: it runs from the
existing maintenance pass (no cron needed), stamps review_request_sent_at
before sending so it never repeats, and skips any order that already has a
review. New migration 018 adds the column + a partial index; the new
review_request template auto-installs on the live DB via syncEmailTemplates.

This completes the customer email journey: order received -> payment
confirmed -> completed (with the delivered code) -> review request.

Verified on real Postgres (8 checks): sent once 24h+ after completion, not for
recently-completed orders, idempotent on a second run, never for orders that
already have a review, and the link targets /track?number=... for that order.
Regression suite (19) + build green.

* Make code-stock auto-delivery reachable everywhere (incl. mobile)

The per-product code inventory + instant auto-delivery already existed on the
backend (paste codes -> a code is auto-claimed, emailed and the order completes
on payment), but the admin UI only exposed it in the desktop table — on a phone
there was no way to add codes at all. Also surfaced it per non-mystery product
so it's clear which items support code delivery:

- Mobile product cards now show a 🔑 stock count and a 'Codes' button that opens
  the same paste-codes modal.
- Desktop 🔑 button now colours by stock (green = has codes, amber = empty) and
  is hidden for mystery boxes (which pay out store credit, not codes).
- Edit modal clarifies the numeric 'Stock cap' vs the 🔑 code stock used for
  instant delivery.

Verified end-to-end on real Postgres (9 checks): pasting codes (dedupes +
strips blanks), order + payment auto-claims one code, delivers + emails it,
completes the order and decrements stock; an order placed with empty stock is
left for manual fulfillment instead of being wrongly completed.

* Add sale pricing (compare-at) with strikethrough price + discount badge

Products can now go on sale: set an original 'was' price and the storefront
shows the current price with the old price struck through and a red -X% badge.
Purely presentational — checkout still charges the real price; the sale price
IS the price, compare-at is display only.

- Stored in metadata.compareAt (cents), surfaced by productService as
  compareAtPrice only when it is genuinely higher than the price (a stale/lower
  value can never render a fake discount).
- Storefront: product cards show a -X% badge (stacked above Featured) + the old
  price struck through; the product page shows price, struck-through original
  and a -X% OFF pill.
- Admin → Products: a 'Sale — original price' field with a live preview of the
  crossed-out price and computed discount %.
- NL translation for the OFF label.

Verified on real Postgres (6 checks): compare-at surfaces only when above the
price (hidden when lower/equal/absent), appears in the public listing, and the
discount math is correct. Screenshots confirm the badge + strikethrough on
cards and the product page. Build green.

* Add per-product delivery mode: Automatic (from stock) vs Manual

Every product now has an explicit delivery choice, so you can automate what you
want and hand-deliver the rest:

- Automatic (default): on payment, a code is pulled from stock, e-mailed and the
  order completes — no action needed.
- Manual: the order is NEVER auto-delivered, even if codes happen to be in
  stock; it waits in the queue and you enter the code per order from the order
  page (which e-mails it and completes the order).

* Fix slow first request (cold start): defer non-critical boot work

Symptom: signup / 'send code' could take ~15s. Cause: ensureReady() — which the
serverless handler awaits before EVERY request on a cold instance — ran heavy
upkeep synchronously on each boot: ~11 email-template queries, per-product art
backfill across the whole catalog (~70+ products), and starter-content dedupe.
On a cold Neon connection those ~100 sequential round-trips stacked up before
the request (and its OTP email) even started.

Now ensureReady only awaits what a request truly needs — migrate (schema),
seed on an empty DB, and stocking an empty catalog — and defers the rest
(syncEmailTemplates upgrade, seedStarterContent, syncCatalogImages) to a
one-shot background task that runs after we're ready to serve.

Measured locally: on an already-seeded DB the blocking boot dropped from doing
~100 queries to 3 (~36ms); on cold Neon that removes the multi-second stall.
The empty-DB path is unchanged (seed() still installs roles/permissions/all
templates synchronously, so auth + OTP work on the very first request).

Verified: boot e2e (6 checks — roles, catalog and login_otp template ready
immediately; 2nd ensureReady memoised; starter box + bundle appear via
background upkeep). Regression (19), lint, build green.

* Supplier listing URLs + serial one-order-at-a-time fulfillment queue

Extends supplier auto-fulfillment so the owner can paste a listing link (e.g. an
Eldorado URL) and paid orders are sourced strictly one at a time, oldest first.

- Migration 021: supplier_products.supplier_url. mapSupplierProduct stores it,
  the admin mapping route + Suppliers.jsx get a 'Listing URL' field, and the
  mapping list shows/links it. The URL is passed into the connector's
  createFulfillment (EldoradoConnector forwards it as listingUrl).
- Serial queue (fulfillmentService): on payment, instead of firing a per-order
  fulfillment, we drain a queue that processes paid supplier orders ONE AT A
  TIME, oldest first — finishing (buy + deliver) one before starting the next.
  A short DB lease (kv row + TTL) guarantees only one worker drains at a time
  across serverless instances; an 'attempted' set advances past orders that open
  no request (margin-guarded) instead of looping; async in-progress buys are
  re-polled from maintenance. Also drained from maintenance as a safety net.

Reality note kept honest in the UI copy: a bare marketplace link can only be
auto-purchased when the connector has a real buy API (Eldorado apiKey); the
queue + link plumbing makes it fully automatic the moment that's configured.

Verified on real Postgres: serial-queue e2e (8 checks — URL stored + passed to
the connector, three paid orders bought strictly oldest-first one at a time, all
completed, a second drain skips under the lease, no double-buying) and the
supplier auto-fulfill e2e (10 checks, incl. the margin-guard order no longer
stalls the queue). Regression (19), lint, build green.

  added to the admin supplier dropdown. The fulfilment request now passes the

Researched G2A and Eneba against their real APIs:

* Audit round: fix payment, coin, and supplier auto-buy money/security bugs

Full audit of the manual-payments, supplier auto-buy, Forge+/coins/wallet,
trust-stats, cold-start and security surfaces. Stats, cold-start, DB
parameterization, admin authz and secret handling verified solid; the
confirmed defects below are fixed and covered by e2e tests.

Payments
- orderService: make the order status transition atomic (conditional UPDATE
  guarded on the observed status + change check). Concurrent confirms / a
  webhook racing a manual confirm can no longer dispense, email or complete an
  order twice.
- paymentProofService: atomically claim a proof (UPDATE ... WHERE status=
  'pending') so a double-click / second admin can't drive a second
  markPaymentReceived; reject non-http(s) screenshot links (zod .url() also
  passes javascript:/data:, a stored-XSS vector in the admin queue); flag the
  2nd proof as multiple_submissions (was off-by-one at the 3rd).
- catalog: reject the screenshot URL at the route too; disable the demo
  self-pay route whenever a real payment method is configured.
- Checkout: show the server order total on the pay-instructions screen — the
  cart is cleared first, so the old cart-derived amount read €0.00.

Forge Coins / membership
- forgeCoinService: lock the user row (FOR UPDATE) before summing in
  spendCoins/redeemReward/grantCoins, matching walletService. Concurrent
  spends can no longer both pass the balance check (negative balance / free
  rewards / free membership).
- account: charge + grant membership in one transaction (no "charged without
  membership", no partial grant).

Supplier auto-buy
- Kinguin/Eldorado: never mark an order fulfilled with zero delivered keys —
  a transient error fetching the keys kept the order in_progress to re-poll
  instead of completing it empty-handed (paid supplier, buyer got nothing).
- fulfillment margin guard: treat an unknown (null) supplier cost as
  do-not-auto-buy, and compare cost to the buyer's effective post-discount
  revenue per unit instead of list price (no blind uncapped buys, no buying at
  a loss on discounted orders).
- G2A: fix the doubled /v3 path prefix (every call 404'd), pass order
  quantity with a line-level max_price cap, and collect multiple keys.

Authentication Bypass For Endpoints With Anonymous Access

Using a remember-me cookie with an arbitrary username can cause Opencast
to assume proper authentication for that user even if the remember-me
cookie was incorrect given that the attacked endpoint also allows
anonymous access.

This way, an attacker can, for example, fake a remember-me token, assume
the identity of the global system administrator and request non-public
content from the search service without ever providing any proper
authentication.

The reason for this problem is that using a remember-me cookie will
always cause the user in the request context to be populated, even if
the cookie is invalid by now. This is usually no problem, except in
combination with anonymous access where anonymous authentication is
granted and the request may continue.

In such a case, Opencast's security service would just check that a user
existed in the request context and assume proper authentication of this
user, never checking if it's actually anonymous authentication.

This patch adds this additional check, falling back to the anonymous
user in case of anonymous authentication.

* feat(orgs): OrganizationInvitation + OrganizationMember entities

The `OrganizationMember` / `OrganizationInvitation` pair that
docs/specs/features/tenants-and-organizations/spec.md §7 defers to v1.1.
Entities and registration only — no behaviour yet.

🛑 organization_members is the ROSTER, not the authorization check. Access
stays `user.tenantId === organization.tenantId` via
OrganizationMembershipService.ensureMember, unchanged. Five independent read
paths depend on that equality (ensureMember, OrganizationService.listForUser,
ScopeOwnershipGuard, TeamsService.listOrgUsers, TeamsService.addMember), and
rewriting them is a far larger change than adding invitations. The table
answers what tenant-equality cannot: who invited this person, when they
joined, and for which Organization — and it is the seam a future per-Org
permission model tightens without a second migration.

Two deliberate tightenings versus the WorkInvitation template:

  - `email` is NOT NULL. WorkInvitation.email is nullable because a Work
    invite can be a bare link handed over out of band. An Org invite exists
    to reach someone with no account, and the mail path silently no-ops on a
    null recipient — nullable would make "invited someone unreachable"
    representable.
  - A partial unique index on (organizationId, emailNormalized) WHERE
    status = 'pending'. Without it, clicking invite twice mints two
    independently redeemable tokens for one mailbox and revoking the visible
    one leaves the other live. Partial, so re-inviting after a revoke or an
    expiry stays legal.

`emailNormalized` is stored rather than derived because the uniqueness index
and the accept-time comparison must agree on one canonical form; computing it
in two places is how "already invited" and "not invited" end up both true.

ORGANIZATION_MEMBER_ROLES has exactly one value on purpose.
OrganizationMembershipService.ensureAdmin is currently
`return this.ensureMember(...)` and its docblock forbids adding a role check
without a product decision, so shipping an `admin` option would put a control
in the UI that grants nothing.

Verified: 54/54 in the database config + module specs. Control: removing
OrganizationMember from _entity-names.ts fails
"entity-names inventory drift (EW-638)", so the registration is genuinely

* feat(orgs): migration for organization_invitations + organization_members

🛑 Why this file gets more scrutiny than most: DATABASE_AUTOMIGRATE (TypeORM
`synchronize`) is TRUE in dev and stage and FALSE in prod — verified on the
live Secrets of ever-works-app-{dev,stage,prod}. In dev and stage,
`synchronize` builds these tables from the entities whether or not this
migration works, so a defect here is invisible in both lower environments and
first appears as a crash-looping prod pod. A green dev rollout is not
evidence for this file.

So it was verified on BOTH engines:

  - Committed spec (better-sqlite3, what CI and e2e run): 4/4 — creation,
    idempotent re-run, down(), and the partial-index behaviour.
  - A throwaway Postgres 16 in Docker, the engine prod actually uses:
    up, up-again, indexes, behaviour, and down all confirmed. The partial
    index is genuinely partial there —
    WHERE ((status)::text = 'pending'::text) — a duplicate PENDING invite is
    rejected, a re-invite after a revoke is accepted, and `id` really does
    default to uuid_generate_v4().

The SQLite pass caught a real defect the Postgres run never would have:
`default: 'now()'` is Postgres-only, and demo/e2e are SQLite. It failed at
INSERT, not at DDL, so the three schema-shape tests passed while the default
was broken. Now CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, matching the house convention in
CreateTeamsTables and AddPluginUsageEvents.

* feat(orgs): invitation token lifecycle — service + repositories

Clones WorkInvitationService's security properties so the two adjacent
features cannot drift: randomBytes(32) token, sha256 stored and the raw value
returned exactly once, lookup by hash so the token never appears in a query,
and a conditional UPDATE for accept so two people redeeming one token resolve
with exactly one winner.

🛑 One deliberate divergence: the ORG token is EMAIL-BOUND, the Work token is
a bearer credential. Accepting an org invitation writes users.tenantId, which
grants access to every Organization in that Tenant — a much larger blast
radius than joining one Work, so a forwarded email must not be enough.
findConsumable() takes the redeemer's address and refuses a mismatch; it stays
optional only for the signed-out preview page, which grants nothing.

normaliseEmail case-folds and trims but deliberately does NOT strip dots or
plus tags. Those are Gmail conventions, not SMTP ones — applying them would
make a.b@corp.com and ab@corp.com the same person on a domain where they are
two different employees.

The 409 for a duplicate invite comes from the partial unique index, not from a
prior SELECT: two clicks a millisecond apart both pass a read-then-write check
and mint two live tokens for one mailbox.

Verified: 19/19. Control: storing the raw token and dropping the email binding
fails exactly 3 tests — "persists ONLY the hash", "refuses a redeemer whose
address is not the invited one", and the prefix case — and nothing else.

The spec also documents a trap it hit: isUniqueConstraintError reads
err.driverError.code, so a test that sets .code on the QueryFailedError
wrapper sails straight past the guard and proves nothing.

* feat(orgs): joinTenant — the single audited writer of a foreign users.tenantId

Accepting an org invitation has to put the invitee in the Organization's
Tenant, because that equality IS the authorization check. This is the third
writer of users.tenantId in the codebase and the only one that ever points a
user at a Tenant somebody else owns, so it lives beside ensureTenant to keep
every write to that column in one audited file.

🛑 It will NOT move a user between Tenants. Hard refusal, not best-effort,
for four independent reasons:

  1. Every row the user already created is stamped with their OLD tenantId by
     ScopeStampingSubscriber and by createOrganization. Repointing orphans all
     of it — the rows keep the old tenant, so their whole history silently
     vanishes from the scope they can now see. Data loss without a DELETE.
  2. tenants.ownerUserId is UNIQUE, so an owner cannot cleanly stop owning;
     repointing leaves an owner-linked, member-less orphan Tenant.
  3. listForUser returns every Org of user.tenantId, so repointing instantly
     hides all of their own Organizations from them.
  4. The FK on users.tenantId is ON DELETE SET NULL — there is no
     database-level protection. The guard must be in code, and tested.

It also deliberately does NOT run createOrganization's TIER_A/TIER_B
backfill: dragging an invitee's pre-existing private rows into the inviter's

   joinTenant COMMITS users.tenantId, and only then did tryAccept run the
   conditional UPDATE. If a revoke landed in that window the claim failed, the
   code threw, and nothing rolled back: the invitee kept TENANT-WIDE access
   with no roster row — invisible in the members list (which reads the roster)
   and not removable via removeMember (which needs one). A revoked invitation
   still granted access.

   My docblock argued for that ordering. It was wrong: it reasoned only about
   the refusal case and never considered a successful join followed by a lost
   claim. Whatever gate authorizes access has to be the atomic one, so the
   claim now runs FIRST and the grant only happens if it wins.

   acceptedByUserId === userId instead of inferring "it was me" from a failed
   re-read, which previously also matched a REVOKED invitation and reported
   success for it.

3. HIGH — joinTenant's check-then-update was a TOCTOU.
   Two invitations accepted at the same instant both observed
   `tenantId IS NULL` and both wrote, homing the user in whichever tenant
   committed last while BOTH invitations were marked accepted. Now a
   conditional UPDATE (UserRepository.claimTenantIfUnassigned,
   WHERE "tenantId" IS NULL) lets the database arbitrate; losing to the SAME
   tenant is idempotent success, losing to a different one is the existing

* fix(conversations): PATCH {"title": null} no longer nulls the title

`@IsOptional()` skips every other validator when the value is `null` as well
as when it is `undefined` — class-validator's condition is literally
`value !== null && value !== undefined`. So `PATCH {"title": null}` sailed
past `@IsString`, then satisfied the handler's `body.title !== undefined`
guard (because `null !== undefined`) and WROTE NULL over the user's title.

It was a hard 400 before the field became optional in #2103, and the DTO's own
docblock still claimed non-string payloads were rejected. They were not.

Replaced with `@ValidateIf(o => o.title !== undefined)`, which restores the
intent exactly: absent is fine, present-but-not-a-string is a 400. Same
treatment for `model`, where a null slipped through to `updateModel` and
happened to coincide with the clear-the-pin branch — harmless, but it made the
documented contract false.

`{}`, never an explicit null.

async def require_cohort_member(
    cohort_id: str,
    user: User,
    db: AsyncSession,
    *roles,
):
    """Verify user is enrolled in the cohort, optionally with required roles."""
    from sqlalchemy import select

    from app.models.cohort import CohortMember

    result = await db.execute(
        select(CohortMember).where(
            CohortMember.cohort_id == cohort_id,
            CohortMember.user_id == user.id,
        )
    )
    member = result.scalar_one_or_none()
    if member is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Not a member of this cohort")
    if roles and member.role not in roles:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Insufficient cohort permissions")
    return member

  — Prisma coi undefined là "không lọc" → trả MỌI user_role → hợp nhất quyền của mọi role

- certificates + grading nhận `AuthPrincipal` và dùng `currentUser.userId`. Bỏ shortcut

  phòng thủ chiều sâu để một chỗ gọi sai không bao giờ thành cấp quyền toàn hệ thống.

explanation:
fix: authorize before cancelling tasks in the chat delete endpoint (#27006)

DELETE /api/v1/chats/{id} called stop_item_tasks(id) before checking the
caller's chat.delete permission or ownership of the target chat. An
authenticated user who knew another user's chat id could therefore cancel that
chat's in-flight generation (streaming response, title or tag generation) even
though the deletion was then rejected. The chat id is discoverable through
legitimate read-only access to a shared chat or folder.

Reorder the handler to authorize first (admin, or owner holding chat.delete) and
only then cancel tasks and delete, matching the dedicated task-stop endpoint.
Legitimate deletions are unchanged; an unauthorized caller now returns 404 or 401
before any cancellation. The duplicated tag-cleanup and event-publish blocks are
merged.

Put the owner's 3D art back, and fix what it sits on (#175)

* admin: action-item count badges in the sidebar (open tickets, pending payments, orders to fulfil)

New GET /api/admin/nav-counts returns open-ticket / pending-payment-proof /
paid-order-awaiting-fulfilment counts; AdminLayout shows a fuchsia badge next
to Support, Payments and Fulfillment (refetched on navigation + every 60s), so
a new ticket is visible at a glance instead of having to hunt for it.

* Per-category delivery explanation on product pages + Discord

Answers the #1 pre-purchase question ('how do I get it?') right on each
product, and mirrors it in Discord.

- src/lib/deliveryInfo.js: bilingual (EN/NL) delivery info per category —
  Robux (Group Payout / Roblox+ method: enable 2FA, 5000 R$/day limit so
  large orders split across days, very large via 2 staff accounts),
  V-Bucks (gift-card code), and a solid code/top-up default.
- ProductDetail: a 'How this is delivered' panel (method + numbered steps +
  good-to-know notes), light-theme styled, with NL labels.
- Discord: /price now shows the delivery method; new /delivery command gives
  the full steps + notes; registered + added to /help.

* admin: one-click suggested sell price from supplier cost

Enter the cost you pay (e.g. on Eldorado/Eneba) and get a 'Suggest price'
button that applies a ~18% markup with a €2 minimum profit, rounded to a
clean .99 — so €140 cost → €165.99, €10 → €11.99. Tune MARKUP/FLOOR in one
place. Existing margin readout stays.

* delivery: drop the Roblox-group join step from Robux (group is only for giveaways)

Robux delivery no longer mentions joining a Roblox group — the group is used
for giveaways, not delivery. Steps are now: enable 2FA → send your username →
we deliver. Updated on the site (EN/NL) and in the Discord bot.

* Forge Coins + Forge Shop, and 'as fast as possible' delivery label

- Forge Coins: a real loyalty currency (append-only ledger, balance = SUM,
  no cached number that can drift). Earn 1 coin per €10 of paid spend,
  awarded once per order (unique index = idempotent on payment retries).
- Forge Shop (account): spend coins on personal discount codes (€5/€10/€25,
  auto-generated single-use coupons) or a giveaway boost. Transactional
  redeem so concurrent spends can't overspend.
- API: GET /account/coins, POST /account/coins/redeem. Nav + route added.
- Migration 012_forge_coins.
- Product page: replaced the 'Estimated delivery ~Xs' line with a simple
  'Delivery: as fast as possible' (NL: 'Levering: zo snel mogelijk').

Verified on real Postgres: earn/idempotency/redeem/overspend all pass; build green.

* Mystery boxes — a real paid 'giveaway' (buy → roll a weighted prize → store credit)

- Migration 013: mystery_box_rewards (weighted prize pool) + mystery_pulls
  (what each buyer won). A mystery box is a product with kind='mystery'.
- mysteryBoxService: weighted roll per unit on payment, pays out as store
  credit via the wallet (tagged = idempotent, no double-pay on retries),
  records the pull + notifies the buyer.
- Hooked into order payment_received.
- Admin: 'Mystery box' toggle + a reward-pool editor (label / odds / € credit)
  in the product modal (GET+PUT /admin/products/:id/mystery).
- Product page: 'What's inside' panel showing every prize + REAL odds.
- Account order page: a celebratory reveal of what you won + credit added.
- Public GET /products/:id/mystery (pool+odds), account GET /orders/:id/mystery.

Verified on real Postgres: roll/credit/record + idempotent re-settle (6/6);
build green. Note: bundles already support any product mix (PS+Xbox, Apex+
Valorant) — create them in Admin → Monetization.

* i18n: Dutch labels for the mystery-box 'What's inside' panel

* Mystery boxes: bulk-luck ('more = better prizes') + a risk-free reroll (1x/box)

- Odds now scale with how many boxes are opened in one order: +8% luck per
  extra box (capped 2x), weighted toward the higher-value prizes — buy more,
  win better. Verified over a large sample (avg prize rises with quantity).
- One reroll per box (migration 014 stamps rerolled_at, claimed atomically so
  it can't be used twice): rolls a fresh prize and the buyer KEEPS the higher
  one — risk-free. POST /account/orders/:id/mystery/:pullId/reroll + a Reroll
  button on the order reveal.

Verified on real Postgres: reroll keeps-the-better + second reroll blocked; build green.

* Drop calendar — scheduled restocks/launches/sales

- Migration 015 + dropService: staff schedule drops (title, category, note,
  date/time); upcoming ones surface on the storefront.
- Public GET /api/drops (upcoming); admin GET/POST/DELETE /api/admin/drops.
- Storefront /drops page (timeline with 'Soon' badges, Discord-alert CTA)
  + a 'Drops' link in the top nav, fully bilingual.
- Admin: a 'Drops' tab in Monetization to schedule/remove drops.
- New drops announce to Discord (best-effort).

Verified on real Postgres (5/5: create/upcoming filter/list/delete); build green.

* Price history chart on product pages

- Migration 016 + price_history: a snapshot on product create and on every
  real price change (dup prices skipped); existing products get a baseline
  point so charts aren't empty.
- Public GET /api/products/:id/price-history.
- Product page: a clean SVG area/line chart with Now + Lowest, and a

Verified on real Postgres (baseline + change tracking + dedup, 3/3); build green.

* Launch polish: surface engagement features + Discord /drops

Site: a 'Save more & win big' section on the homepage with cards linking to
Forge Coins, Mystery boxes and the Drop calendar — so the new features are
actually discoverable (bilingual).

Discord: new /drops command showing the upcoming drop calendar (live from the
store, with Discord relative timestamps) + a link to the full calendar;
registered and added to /help.

* Live trust stats: refresh instantly on delivery + new review (no fabrication)

The trust stats (delivered count, customers, review count, average rating) are
already computed 100% from real DB rows — nothing seeded or padded (demoSeed
only inserts products; no hardcoded numbers in the UI). This makes them update
INSTANTLY instead of within the 15s cache window: bust the social/stats cache
the moment an order is marked delivered and the moment a review is added, so
the counters and average rating move up right away.

Verified on real Postgres: delivered increments on completion, review count +
rating reflect a real review; boots with no circular-import issue.

* Launch-ready hardening: zero-admin setup, critical fixes, self-running maintenance

Critical fixes:
- productSchema rejected kind='mystery' (enum was digital|physical) → the
  admin's Mystery box toggle could never save. Added 'mystery'.
- Admin fulfillment badge counted status='paid', which doesn't exist →

  now ok by default (cron stays as optional backup).
- Starter content on first boot (idempotent, never overwrites admin work):
  the €49.99 Forge Mystery Box with a balanced 5-prize pool (EV ≈ €38.75 →

  10% off). 'mystery' category gets its own card visual.

- Mystery-only orders now AUTO-COMPLETE on payment (the credit payout IS

add-order body incl. product_id/currency/max_price, pay step, key→delivery,

* Audit round: fix payment, coin, and supplier auto-buy money/security bugs

Full audit of the manual-payments, supplier auto-buy, Forge+/coins/wallet,
trust-stats, cold-start and security surfaces. Stats, cold-start, DB
parameterization, admin authz and secret handling verified solid; the
confirmed defects below are fixed and covered by e2e tests.

Payments
- orderService: make the order status transition atomic (conditional UPDATE
  guarded on the observed status + change check). Concurrent confirms / a
  webhook racing a manual confirm can no longer dispense, email or complete an
  order twice.
- paymentProofService: atomically claim a proof (UPDATE ... WHERE status=
  'pending') so a double-click / second admin can't drive a second
  markPaymentReceived; reject non-http(s) screenshot links (zod .url() also
  passes javascript:/data:, a stored-XSS vector in the admin queue); flag the
  2nd proof as multiple_submissions (was off-by-one at the 3rd).
- catalog: reject the screenshot URL at the route too; disable the demo
  self-pay route whenever a real payment method is configured.
- Checkout: show the server order total on the pay-instructions screen — the
  cart is cleared first, so the old cart-derived amount read €0.00.

Forge Coins / membership
- forgeCoinService: lock the user row (FOR UPDATE) before summing in
  spendCoins/redeemReward/grantCoins, matching walletService. Concurrent
  spends can no longer both pass the balance check (negative balance / free
  rewards / free membership).
- account: charge + grant membership in one transaction (no "charged without
  membership", no partial grant).

Supplier auto-buy
- Kinguin/Eldorado: never mark an order fulfilled with zero delivered keys —
  a transient error fetching the keys kept the order in_progress to re-poll
  instead of completing it empty-handed (paid supplier, buyer got nothing).
- fulfillment margin guard: treat an unknown (null) supplier cost as
  do-not-auto-buy, and compare cost to the buyer's effective post-discount
  revenue per unit instead of list price (no blind uncapped buys, no buying at
  a loss on discounted orders).
- G2A: fix the doubled /v3 path prefix (every call 404'd), pass order
  quantity with a line-level max_price cap, and collect multiple keys.

* Semi-automate fulfillment: auto-surface paid orders, enrich the manual queue

Turns the "manual" tier into a semi-automatic one and closes a gap where paid
orders that can't be delivered automatically could sit invisible.

Automatic (unchanged): local code-stock auto-dispense and Kinguin/G2A supplier
auto-buy still deliver hands-off.

Auto-surface (new)
- fulfillmentService.ensureManualFulfillment: a paid order with no stock and no
  auto-supplier (e.g. a P2P Robux/V-Bucks top-up) is now queued for hand
  delivery instead of sitting at payment_received with no fulfillment request.
  Advances the order to awaiting_fulfillment (same path fulfillOrder walks) so
  completing the manual request can legally complete the order. Idempotent.
- Wired into the payment_received handler (after stock + supplier drain) and
  into maintenance as a backfill sweep (sweepUnfulfilledPaidOrders) for orders
  paid before this path existed or missed by an interrupted drain.

Semi-automatic manual queue
- listManualQueue now returns, per request: the supplier listing URL to buy
  from (supplier_url), the quantity, and the buyer's delivery target captured
  at checkout. Admin Fulfillment page shows a "Buy from supplier" link, the
  quantity, and the copy-able delivery target — buy, paste the code, one click
  delivers + e-mails the buyer.
- Capture the delivery target at checkout: products can define a deliveryField
  label (e.g. "Roblox username", set in the admin product form); Checkout shows
  a required field only when a cart item needs it and stores it on the order,
  sanitized server-side.

Robustness
- resolveFulfillmentSupplier skips a supplier whose connector kind is unknown/
  removed instead of throwing, so one bad supplier row can't abort the drain
  for every order.

Verified on local Postgres: new semi-auto e2e 10/10 (auto-surface, queue shows
buy link + qty + target, one-click deliver completes + records, idempotent),
supplier 10/10, queue 8/8, regression 19/19, npm run build green.

* Surface margin-guarded orders for review + Discord bot audit fixes

Margin-guarded orders (server)
- autoFulfillFromSuppliers: when the margin guard refuses a buy (supplier cost
  unknown or >= effective revenue), the order is now queued for hand delivery
  via a shared queueForHandDelivery helper instead of being left with no
  fulfillment request. Previously it sat invisible while the serial drain
  re-picked it on every run; now the owner sees it in the manual queue (with
  the supplier listing link) and decides: buy anyway or refund.
- ensureManualFulfillment refactored onto the same helper (behaviour unchanged).

Discord bot (audit findings)
- /vouch could push unlimited 5-star reviews to the storefront: externalId was
  keyed to the interaction id, defeating the server-side dedup. Now keyed to
  the user (one site review per member) plus a 1-hour per-user cooldown.
- Giveaway duration clamped to 1 min - 14 days: larger values overflow Node's
  32-bit timer and ended the giveaway after 1ms (also on restart re-arm).
- Live price list: stop adding embed fields near Discord's 6000-char total cap
  so a large catalog can't make the update throw and silently freeze the list.
- Ticket "one open ticket" check now matches the owner id with its trailing
  delimiter, so a member whose snowflake prefixes another's is not blocked.
- getProducts: 8s fetch timeout + cache-stamped backoff so a hanging API can't
  stall every /price, /ask and price-list refresh with piled-up sockets.
- Review ingest: stop sending the raw shared secret as a legacy header; the
  HMAC-signed path is the only transport.

Verified: margin-queue e2e 5/5 (order surfaces with buy link, drain stops
re-picking, no auto duplicates), supplier 10/10, queue 8/8, semiauto 10/10,
regression 19/19, audit-fix 9/9, npm run build green, node --check on bot files.

* Email security + reliability fixes, cart-sync race, silent sign-in repair

Email (audit findings)
- renderTokens now HTML-escapes every token value unless the token name ends
  in Html (itemsHtml, deliveriesHtml, paymentHtml, noteHtml, codeHtml — all
  server-built with their own escaping). Previously billing.full_name flowed
  raw into branded emails, letting a guest checkout deliver attacker HTML to
  any address from our verified sender (phishing relay). billing.full_name and
  city are also bounded at order creation.
- deliverOrder: sending codes to an ALREADY completed order (replacement code)
  now emails the customer explicitly — the completed→completed transition
  early-returns, so the codes previously landed silently with no email/DM.
- retryFailedEmails maintenance sweep: transactional emails that failed on a
  transient provider error are re-sent from their persisted context (atomic
  claim, capped attempts per recipient so a dead address ages out). Wired as
  maintenance step 10. Previously a 10s Resend timeout on order_completed
  meant a guest never received their codes and nothing ever retried.
- assertProductionConfig: no more false "emails not delivered" warning when
  Resend is configured without SMTP_URL.

Frontend (audit findings)
- CartContext: the server-cart mirror now waits until the login restore has
  settled (a slow cold-start GET raced the 900ms mirror, which PUT an empty
  local cart over the saved one), and the restore uses a functional update so
  an item added while the GET was in flight is never replaced by a stale
  server cart.
- AuthContext: a stale fm_token no longer strands a returning customer as a
  guest — on a failed /me the token is cleared and the silent sign-in ladder
  (refresh cookie, then trusted device) is retried.
- i18n: NL translations for the checkout delivery-target field
  (checkout.deliveryPh / checkout.deliveryHint).

Verified: new email-fix e2e 11/11 (escaping + *Html passthrough, injected
full_name recorded escaped, retry sweep claims + re-sends exactly once,
replacement delivery emails again), regression 19/19, supplier 10/10, queue
8/8, semiauto 10/10, marginqueue 5/5, npm run build green.

* Self-healing Discord invite: bot maintains a permanent link, site serves it live

A default Discord invite expires after 7 days — a dead link on the storefront
silently kills community sign-ups. This closes that hole end to end:

Bot
- ensurePermanentInvite: on boot (and re-checked daily) the bot finds an
  existing never-expiring invite (maxAge 0, unlimited uses) or creates one on
  the most public channel it can invite from, then pushes it to the site over
  the same HMAC-signed transport as the other bot endpoints (the URL is bound
  into the signature). A manually-deleted invite heals itself within a day.
- /invite command now hands out the maintained permanent link instead of a
  hardcoded one.

Server
- POST /api/discord/invite (HMAC-signed, replay-windowed): accepts only real
  discord.gg / discord.com/invite URLs and stores the link in kv.
- getLiveInviteUrl/setLiveInviteUrl in discordService; getServerInfo now
  serves the live link first, falling back to the env-configured invite.

Frontend
- Drops page uses the live invite from /api/discord/server instead of a
  hardcoded link (the Discord page already read it from the API).

Verified: new invite e2e 8/8 (signed push accepted; bad signature, stale
timestamp, non-Discord URL and URL-swap all rejected; live link served and
replaceable), regression 19/19, npm run build green, node --check on the bot.

* Payment-proof Discord ping, mobile overflow fixes, e2e suites + CI

Three launch-readiness improvements:

Payment-proof ping (manual payments confirm as fast as the owner reacts)
- discordService.postPaymentProofAlert: the moment a customer submits payment
  proof, staff get a Discord embed (order, amount, method, transaction id,

  hiccup never blocks the submission.

Mobile fixes (390px sweep of every customer page; two real overflows found)
- Home header: gap-6 across all items burned ~96px of width on phones,

  Sign Up (arrow hidden on xs). Page fits 390px exactly.
- Checkout steps: four full labels + connectors overflowed 390px; on phones
  only the active step keeps its label. Shop, product, pay, track, cart and

Tests in-repo + CI
- server/test/: the ten e2e suites (audit fixes, semiauto fulfillment,

  queue, kinguin/g2a/guard connectors) with relative imports, plus

Verified: npm test → all 10 suites green locally; proof alert lands in
discord_outbox with order number + admin link; mobile re-sweep shows
scrollWidth == clientWidth on both fixed pages; npm run build green.

* Delivery choice (gift code vs account top-up) + email order summary + price-bug fix

Delivery choice
- Products can offer the buyer a choice at checkout: a gift code (emailed) or a
  direct top-up to their account (like a Roblox top-up). Product form gets a
  "let the buyer choose" toggle next to the delivery-target label; when off but
  a target is set, the account target stays mandatory (pure top-up product).
- Checkout shows the choice only when a cart item offers it; picking "account"
  reveals the required target field. The pick is stored as billing.deliveryMethod
  ('code' | 'account'); a supplied target implies account delivery (backward
  compatible with the pre-choice checkout).
- Account top-ups are ALWAYS hand-delivered — autoDispenseFromStock skips them so

  the code field (owner just confirms).

Emails
- The order summary now renders a real breakdown (subtotal, each discount, store
  credit, bold total) — fixes the mismatch where a line item showed the list
  price (€9.99) but the total showed the discounted amount (€4.49) with no

- The completion email hero is method-aware: a premium copyable code card for
  code orders, or a green "delivered straight to your account" confirmation
  (with the username, no code) for top-ups. All inline-styled so it survives

- New renderOrderEmail() helper renders an order email to {subject, html} for

the queue, completes on confirm, email shows the account confirmation without

* Premium order_completed email (Clean Premium Receipt), auto-upgrade on deploy

Redesigns the order-complete email into a premium, fully inline-styled layout
(status pills, "Your loot is ready" hero, the delivery hero, a labelled Order
summary breakdown, gradient CTA, support line) — inline styles survive clients
that strip <style>. Direction chosen via a design panel (3 directions judged).

The previous default body is added to LEGACY_TEMPLATE_BODIES so syncEmailTemplates
upgrades existing installs whose stored template is still the old default (an
admin-customized template is left untouched).

* Set the permanent Discord invite (discord.gg/CrAfqENsSV) as the fallback

Replaces the old invite everywhere it's hardcoded as a fallback — env config,
the bot's /invite fallback, and the storefront community + drops pages. The
live bot still keeps a never-expiring invite in sync on top of this once it runs.

* Replace Orbitron headings with Space Grotesk (cleaner, premium)

Community feedback: the display font read as "ugly". Swaps the loud sci-fi
Orbitron heading font for Space Grotesk — modern, premium, still with a tech/
gaming character and much more legible. Keeps Inter for body and Rajdhani for
small uppercase labels. The legacy `font-orbitron` Tailwind token is aliased to
the new display font so no element ever requests an unloaded typeface.
Chosen by rendering candidates (Orbitron vs Space Grotesk vs Sora) side by side.

* Mystery box: hide the odds — keep it a mystery

Removes the visible win-percentages on the mystery-box product page (the prize
list stays, so buyers still see what they can win). The weights/odds are no
longer sent to the client at all, so the chances can't be read from devtools
either — the mystery stays a mystery. Admin still manages weights as before.

* Fix: custom product Image URL no longer reset to the default icon

The catalog art sync ran on every boot and forced each demo product's image
back to its shipped 3D icon — so an Image URL set in Admin → Products saved,
then got overwritten on the next deploy/cold start. Both the boot-time
syncCatalogImages and the demo-seed backfill now only set the default cover
when the product has NO image; an owner-set image is always preserved. Clearing
the Image URL field falls back to the default icon again (a natural reset).

* Admin products: search + bulk-set one image across a selection

Adds a search box to the products list (matches name / category / SKU) and a
"select all matches" shortcut — so you can type "robux", grab every variant,
and apply ONE image URL to the whole selection in a single click. Select-all
now operates on the filtered matches.

The bulk endpoint gains an `image` action: sets (or clears, with an empty
value) metadata.image across every selected product; only real http(s) URLs are
accepted. Combined with the earlier fix, an owner-set image now sticks.

* Premium logo plinth behind product images (uniform for any logo)

Adds a reusable .fm-logo-plinth tray + .fm-logo treatment: a soft rounded
background with a subtle violet glow disc and an inner ring, and a drop shadow
on the image. Mixed product logos — transparent PNGs or badge-style marks —
now read as one cohesive, premium set. Applied to the home Popular Products
tiles and the storefront product cards (LightProductCard).

* Headings: Space Grotesk → Bricolage Grotesque (more character, premium)

Final type polish. Bricolage Grotesque gives the headings a warmer, more
"designed" editorial feel than the plainer Space Grotesk, while staying modern
and highly legible. Body stays Inter, small labels stay Rajdhani; the legacy
display token aliases follow. Chosen by rendering candidates (Space Grotesk vs
Bricolage vs Outfit vs Sora) with the real fonts and the actual hero text.

* Hero glow-up: coloured halos behind each floating logo + livelier float

Gives each hero logo a soft brand-tinted glow halo (the signature look of the
target mockup) and a livelier, varied up-and-down float with gentle rotation
(three staggered variants + a breathing halo). Bigger logos, fuller arrangement,
stronger podium glow. The logos already load from the icon PNGs, so once real
brand PNGs are dropped in they appear here automatically — floating, haloed.
Respects prefers-reduced-motion. Build green; rendered on desktop + mobile.

* Fallback to category logo when a product image fails to load

A missing or 404'ing product image showed the browser's ugly broken-image
placeholder over the gradient. Product detail hero and storefront cards now
detect the load error (onError) and render the category logo centred on the
gradient instead.

* Product images: Pinterest links + gallery upload; smarter search

Images:
- Owner can upload a product image straight from their device/gallery. The
  file is downscaled + inlined as a data URI (no blob store needed), on both
  the product editor and the bulk 'one image for the whole selection' toolbar.
- Pasting a page link (e.g. a Pinterest pin) now resolves to the real image
  behind it via a new admin resolve-image endpoint (og:image / twitter:image),
  with an SSRF guard blocking internal hosts.
- Image values are validated centrally (isSafeImageValue): site paths, http(s)
  links and raster data URIs are allowed; javascript:/svg/html URIs rejected.

Search:
- Storefront (command palette + shop filter) and the admin product search now
  ignore case, spaces and punctuation, so 'vbucks' matches 'V-Bucks'.

Tests: new imageUrl unit suite (safe-value, SSRF guard, og:image, resolver
via mock fetch) + a data-URI acceptance case in the bulk-image suite.

* Fit owner-supplied product images cleanly into card & hero

An uploaded/linked image with its own (often white) background showed as a
hard box floating on the tile. Custom images (isCustomImage: not /products/*)
now render as a contained logo over a soft blurred backdrop of themselves, so
the background blends edge-to-edge instead of clipping or floating. Built-in
pack/category logos keep their plinth treatment.

Note: on the card the artwork is force-positioned relative by .fm-card-media,
and a % max-height there resolves against the auto grid track (ignored), so the
size cap uses fixed px.

* Fix: uploaded product images larger than 1mb now save

Uploading a real photo/logo silently failed to save — the base64 image
exceeded Express' 1mb JSON body limit, so the request 413'd and the product
never changed. Raised the body limit to 3mb (still guarded by isSafeImageValue,
now capped at 2.5mb) and made the client encoder compress uploads: photos are
re-encoded as JPEG with a size budget (PNG kept only when the image truly has
transparency), so a phone-sized image lands well under the limit.

Adds a large-image regression test (1.4mb saves, oversized → 400, bulk too).

Two things made saving an image feel broken even though it saved:
- The admin Products list rows always rendered a fixed category icon, never

megabyte each. They now come from a generator (scripts/gen-icons.mjs) that

Harden human review and blind freeze governance (#17)

* test(freeze): cover the one-way human blind-v3 freeze contract

freeze_human_blind_v3.py had no test importing it at all, despite being
the only irreversible step on the path out of QUALIFIED_SHADOW: it
hashes a selected human-adjudicated set and commits those samples to
FROZEN. Every comparable path in the repository — backup rotation,
release audit, migration restore, light verification — already has a
contract test.

The fixture builds an adjudicated corpus sitting exactly at the
production minimums (30 RISK_REVIEW / 30 NON_TARGET / 20 ABSTAIN across
four source families, one distinct issuer, chain, passage and text hash
per event). Sitting at the minimum is deliberate: excluding a single
event must then break the freeze, which is what proves --exclude-jsonl
reaches the selector instead of being read and discarded.

Pinned invariants:
- a candidate build writes the dataset and manifest but leaves every
  sample READY, carries no rows inside the manifest, and reports zero
  entity, chain, exact-text and near-duplicate overlap
- the same corpus yields the same freeze id and the same dataset bytes
- artifacts are written atomically, owner-only, leaving no .tmp behind
- --apply refuses an absent authorization id, actor, expiry, or a
  purpose under twenty characters, and refuses an expired one
- every refusal leaves all samples unfrozen and writes no manifest, so
  no artifact can later be mistaken for an authorized freeze receipt
- an authorized apply freezes exactly the selected samples under the
  manifest freeze id, records the authorization, and reports the model
  and canonical ledger as unchanged
- a second authorized run cannot re-freeze or re-identify the set
- the exclusion loader normalizes hash case, skips blank lines, rejects
  a non-object row, and collects all seven overlap dimensions

Each guard was mutation-checked: removing the authorization test, the
expiry test, the missing-reference test, the exclusion wiring, or the
freeze call itself turns the corresponding tests red.

Coverage of the script goes from 0% to 99%; suite is 719 passed with 21
subtests.

One observation left unpinned for review: the dataset file is written
before the --apply authorization check, so a refused commit can leave a
dataset with no manifest beside it. The tests assert the safety
invariants (nothing frozen, no manifest) without fixing that ordering
in place, so reordering it later stays a deliberate choice.

Talos worker nodes use `trustd` API on control plane nodes to issue
certificates for `apid` service. Access to the API is protected with the

authentication with any set of Talos API RBAC roles, including
`os:admin` role allowing full access to the Talos API on control plane
nodes.

+
+## Normalizing the email address
+
+By default, NextAuth.js will normalize the email address. It treats values as case-insensitive (which is technically not compliant to the [RFC 2821 spec](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2821), but in practice this causes more problems than it solves, eg. when looking up users by e-mail from databases.) and also removes any secondary email address that was passed in as a comma-separated list. You can apply your own normalization via the `normalizeIdentifier` method on the `EmailProvider`. The following example shows the default behavior:
+```ts
+  EmailProvider({
+    // ...
+    normalizeIdentifier(identifier: string): string {
+      // Get the first two elements only,
+      // separated by `@` from user input.
+      let [local, domain] = identifier.toLowerCase().trim().split("@")
+      // The part before "@" can contain a ","
+      // but we remove it on the domain part
+      domain = domain.split(",")[0]
+      return `${local}@${domain}`
+
+      // You can also throw an error, which will redirect the user
+      // to the error page with error=EmailSignin in the URL
+      // if (identifier.split("@").length > 2) {
+      //   throw new Error("Only one email allowed")
+      // }
+    },
+  })
+```
+
+:::warning
+Always make sure this returns a single e-mail address, even if multiple ones were passed in.
+:::

Changelog

1.9.3 - `unreleased`
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
- Fixed arbitrary certificate revocation at the CA (`GHSA-pxmc-2ffp-8j67`_). Certificate identity was tracked
  only by Lemur's internal database row, not by the actual CA-side certificate. Any authenticated subject could
  upload a duplicate record for a certificate they didn't own (matching an existing ``authority_id`` and
  ``serial``) and then revoke it via ``PUT /api/1/certificates/<id>/revoke``, causing the CA to revoke the
  real certificate belonging to another subject. ``POST /api/1/certificates/upload`` now requires
  ``AuthorityPermission`` on the specified authority, and rejects uploads whose ``(authority_id, serial)``
  pair already matches an existing certificate with a ``409`` response. ``PUT /api/1/certificates/<id>/revoke``
  now also checks authorization and endpoint attachment against every certificate row sharing
  ``(authority_id, serial)`` with the one being revoked, not just the row named in the request, closing the
  gap for any duplicate rows that already exist.

An authenticated member of one project can modify and delete members of
another project, without knowledge of this other project's private
code. This can be further exploited to access all bills of another project
without knowledge of this other project's private code.

authenticated and exploit this flaw. As such, the exposure is similar to
an unauthenticated attack, because it is trivial to become authenticated.

fix(red-team): address 8 security vulnerabilities from Red Team audit

1. ATTACK-01: Fake promo codes → database-backed validation with PromoCode model + migration 021
2. ATTACK-04: XSS in email → html.escape() + URL scheme validation on all user-controlled fields
3. ATTACK-05: CSRF bypass → extended CSRF protection to all mutating endpoints (with webhook/auth exempts)
4. ATTACK-06: Entitlement race condition → atomic UPDATE with WHERE clause (consumed+qty <= quantity)
5. ATTACK-09: IDOR in prompt compiler → pass user_id to compile_prompt, verify project ownership
6. ATTACK-15: Mock payment mode → startup guard raises if YOOKASSA creds missing in production
7. ATTACK-16: Audit log silent bypass → changed logger.debug to logger.warning
8. ATTACK-19: Missing security headers → added SecurityHeadersMiddleware (HSTS, X-Frame-Options, etc.)
9. ATTACK-20: Contact import validation → added input validation, length limits, date parsing, contacts limit

RED TEAM SCORE: 22/100 → estimated improvement to 65/100

feat(membership): the non-self-writable admission record, its predicates and spec (#891)

* feat(membership): the non-self-writable admission record, its predicates and spec

Part of epic #801 (PRD Phase 3, harden multi-event isolation). Spec + types
only: no firestore.rules, no storage.rules, no functions/**, no UI. Five child
tickets consume this contract, so it lands first as one shape rather than five.

The invariant: a gate the reader can satisfy by writing its own admission
record is not a gate. Every candidate record today is exactly that —
players/{uid} is `allow create, update: if isOwner(uid) || isAdmin(eventId)`
with no membership precondition (firestore.rules:1007-1008), so any signed-in
account mints its own row under any Event id and passes its own gate. #844
reached the same finding independently from PR #838's review.

- specs/event-membership.md — the contract: the record at
  events/{eventId}/memberships/{uid} with the uid as the document id, the
  Admin-SDK-only write path, the role model, the shared predicate for both
  rules files, the document-access budget, the enforced-path inventory, the
  per-Event enforcement switch, and the nine epic decisions split into
  answered-by-the-code and needs-the-owner.
- src/domainTypes.d.ts — MembershipDoc, MembershipRole, MembershipStatus,
  MembershipEnforcement, AdmissionDecision, and EventDoc.membershipEnforcement.
- src/data/eventMembership.ts — the pure predicates, importable by the client,
  the Functions and the rules suites; no Firebase import.
- CONTEXT.md — Membership as a new noun, with Player narrowed to a stats row.

Three budget findings the rules tickets would otherwise hit at the emulator:
the reshuffle board write already costs 9 of its 10 document-access calls, so
the gate must ride the create arm and not the mutation; the events/{eventId}
rule cannot absorb the one expression that holds the switch immutable, making
#850 a prerequisite of #804; and Storage allows only two Firestore documents
per evaluation, which is what fixes the switch onto the Event document.

Closes #802

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(membership): keep admission on board updates; the Functions consume a mirror

Codex round 1 on PR #891.

P1 (blocking) — the `resource != null || admitted(eventId)` shape let a revoked
member keep marking and reshuffling a board they had already dealt, which
contradicts this spec's own definition of revocation as stopping future writes.
Withdrawn entirely, along with the "gate the create, not the mutation"
generalisation, which has the same hole wherever it is applied.

The budget is recovered by removing redundant reads instead. Two refactors
prescribed for #804: hoist the Event document (isAdmin, the unlockAt read and
the enforcement switch all fetch the same doc separately), and parameterise the
reshuffle counter (`getAfter(playerDoc).data.reshufflesUsed` is evaluated four
times, twice of them inside the path `reshuffleSpendMarkerDoc` returns). The
reshuffle path then costs 7 of 10 WITH the gate on both arms — cheaper than the
8-9 it costs today. The double-charges, not the membership gate, were the
budget problem.

P2 — the Functions cannot import `src/data/eventMembership.ts`:
`functions/tsconfig.json` sets `rootDir: "src"`, so a runtime cross-tree import
fails TS6059. Verified against the Functions compiler with a throwaway probe,
not assumed. The two existing `../../src/` imports are `import type` from a
declaration-only `.d.ts` and emit nothing, so they are not a precedent. #803
adds `functions/src/membershipVocab.ts` on the established mirror pattern
(`functions/src/scoringVocab.ts` + `tests/functions/finale-parity.test.ts`)
rather than relaxing rootDir.

Also self-caught: the nine access calls belong to the enclosing `boards` clause,
not to `reshuffleOk()` (which costs seven), and the owner path costs eight.

* fix(membership): deny unauthenticated callers; validate revocation as a pair

Codex round 1 on PR #891, the two findings the poll tail had truncated.

P2 — `admits()` answered from `enforcement` alone, so it would have admitted an
UNAUTHENTICATED caller for every Event in the dark-rollout state, which is every
Event today. The rules predicate it mirrors leads with `signedIn()`; the mirror
did not. It now takes the caller's uid and denies its absence first, before the
enforcement switch is consulted. An unenforced Event is open to every signed-in
account, never to the public.

Deliberately does NOT compare that uid against the record's own `uid`: the
document path already encodes it and the rules perform no such comparison, so
adding one would be a divergence in the other direction.

P2 — `readMembership` accepted half-applied revocations, silently dropping an
unusable `revokedAt`/`revokedBy` or retaining a stale one beside an active
status, handing consumers a "parsed" revocation with no author and no date.
Both fields are now validated as a status-dependent pair in both directions.

Kept strictly as a PARSE decision: `admits` still reads `status` alone, so an
inconsistent revoked record still denies and an inconsistent active one still
admits, exactly as the rules would. A test pins that, because tightening the
parse must never move the admission answer or the reference stops mirroring the
rules it is supposed to be checked against.
