feat: durable encrypted delegate queue for background local_delegate (v1.6.0) (#61)

* feat: add queue_server.py, a durable encrypted delegate queue service

Standalone PEP 723 service (stdlib + pinned cryptography) intended to
run on JVMBPro as a LaunchAgent in front of the local Ollama:

- HTTP JSON API on 127.0.0.1:11438 (QUEUE_PORT/QUEUE_UPSTREAM env):
  POST /v1/jobs (validated chat payload, ~2 MB cap, returns a
  q-prefixed uuid4hex job id), GET /v1/jobs/<id> (status),
  GET /v1/jobs/<id>/result (persists until TTL — deliberately NOT
  single-collect), DELETE /v1/jobs/<id> (cancel), GET /healthz.
- SQLite (WAL) at ~/.local/state/delegate-queue/queue.db, dir 0700,
  files 0600. Payloads and results are AES-256-GCM blobs with a fresh
  nonce per encryption; only job metadata is plaintext columns.
- Key: 32 bytes, base64 in the System keychain (DELEGATE_QUEUE_KEY /
  jasonvassallo), read once at startup. Fail closed: no key, no
  service. Key material and payload contents are never logged.
- Worker: 2 concurrent jobs, 1800 s ceiling, crash recovery
  (running -> queued on startup) with a 2-attempt cap, 72 h TTL sweep
  at startup and hourly.

This intentionally reverses the "no delegated jobs on disk" rule with
user approval (2026-08-07); encryption at rest is the mitigation. The
worker is a 2-thread pool rather than the sketched async loop — stdlib
http.server is thread-based and stdlib asyncio has no HTTP server —
with identical concurrency semantics.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: queue-first background delegation in local_delegate

Client side of the durable queue (stdlib-only additions):

- Queue endpoint chain: default (http://localhost:11438,
  https://queue-mbp.djvassallo.com), AI_TOOLS_QUEUE_URLS CSV override,
  every entry validated by the same fail-closed rules as the Ollama
  chain. Auth reuses _ollama_auth_headers — the same CF Access service
  token gates the queue hostname, and a remote endpoint with no
  credentials is skipped, never called bare.
- local_delegate(background=true) probes /healthz (~2 s) and submits to
  the first healthy queue endpoint, returning the q-prefixed job id
  with "queue": "durable" in the envelope. No queue reachable -> the
  in-memory path runs unchanged with a "warning" field naming the
  non-durable fallback (composed with any think/model advisory).
- local_delegate_result routes q-prefixed ids to the queue (running
  envelope, stored answer through the existing renderer, retryable
  error when the queue is unreachable since the job is durable
  server-side); legacy 32-hex ids keep the in-memory path untouched.
- Tool descriptions and the module docstring document durable vs
  fallback semantics.

Four background tests in test_local_delegate.py now see the queue-first
path and go red at this commit; the following test commit updates them
alongside the new queue coverage.

- test_local_delegate.py: queue chain resolution/validation, healthz

* fix: batched remediation for the queue-service review findings (PR #61)

One authorized convergence-budget batch on top of ecfa3b6, addressing
the verified P1/P2 findings from the CodeRabbit/Codex review cycle:

queue_server.py
- Worker threads can no longer be killed by ANY exception class. The
  documented failure: http.client.IncompleteRead (an HTTPException, not
  an OSError) escaping _work_one's except chain terminated the thread
  permanently, silently stranding all future queued jobs. _work_one now
  has a terminal `except Exception` that marks the job failed with
  error_class=worker_error (message carries only the exception CLASS
  name, never content), and _run wraps each loop iteration so even a
  store failure in claim_next logs, backs off, and continues.
- Submit-time backpressure: MAX_QUEUED=64; a submit beyond the cap
  draws HTTP 429 inside a BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction (queued jobs are
  TTL-exempt, so the cap is what bounds backlog growth).
- cancel() now runs BEGIN IMMEDIATE with a status-guarded UPDATE and a
  rowcount check: previously its unguarded UPDATE could overwrite a
  `done` row committed by finish() between cancel's SELECT and UPDATE.
  finish() already refused to overwrite cancelled rows; now the race is
  closed in both directions.
- result() for administratively-failed jobs (attempts cap, crash
  recovery) now says what happened ("failed after exhausting N of 2
  attempts...") instead of "job finished without a result".

mcp_server.py
- _queue_submit distinguishes safe fallback from AMBIGUOUS outcomes.
  Connect errors and HTTP error statuses (job provably not enqueued)
  still fall back to the in-memory store; a read timeout / dropped
  connection after the request was sent, or an HTTP 200 without a
  usable job_id, now raise instead — falling back there could execute
  the same prompt twice (queue worker + in-memory). The background
  handler surfaces that as a clean tool error, never a duplicate run.
- _queue_poll walks EVERY configured queue endpoint on 404 instead of
  declaring the job purged after asking only the first healthy one:
  each endpoint has an independent store, so "unknown here" also
  covers a job whose accepting endpoint is currently unreachable. The
  all-404 error now names the endpoints and both possibilities.
- Implicit-model background jobs that land on the durable queue carry
  a warning: the model was resolved against this machine's Ollama
  chain, but the queue executes against its own upstream, which may
  not serve the tag (full endpoint-affinity resolution deferred —
  ledgered, needs new queue API surface).

Docs/CI
- README.md drops the stale "nothing written to disk / no persistent
  background service" claims and describes the durable queue honestly:
  AES-256-GCM at rest, System-keychain key, 72 h TTL, opt-in by
  deployment, in-memory path remains the fallback.
- prerelease-guard now also checks the delegate-queue LaunchAgent
  plist for the UV_PRERELEASE pin (multiline-aware, since plist XML
  splits key and value across lines).
- DEPLOY.md cloudflared ingress uses 127.0.0.1 literally, matching
  make_server()'s IPv4-only bind.

test_queue_server.py / test_local_delegate.py
- Regression tests for every fix above (worker survives IncompleteRead
  and arbitrary exceptions plus a claim_next crash; 429 at the cap;
  attempts_exhausted result text; cancel/finish thread race; ambiguous
  vs safe submit fallback; 404 chain walk; envelope warnings).
- CI raw-socket 400 test reads the response to EOF instead of a single
  recv(4096): BaseHTTPRequestHandler writes headers and body
  separately, so one recv could return the headers alone and lose the
  body assertion on slow CI runners (passed 30/30 under repetition).

* fix(queue): read the System keychain explicitly; make DEPLOY.md runnable and safe to publish

queue_server.py (CRITICAL): load_key_from_system_keychain() built a
find-generic-password argv with no keychain path. macOS then searches
the caller's keychain list, which resolves login.keychain-db before
/Library/Keychains/System.keychain — the store DEPLOY.md provisions and
verifies. The shadowing is already demonstrated on JVMBPro for sibling
secrets (CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN exist in both
stores and pathless lookups return the login copy). In the gui/501
domain the service could therefore load the WRONG key, start cleanly,
and then fail authenticated decryption on every stored job. Pass
/Library/Keychains/System.keychain explicitly, still failing closed, and
name that path in the not-found error so a wrong-store miss is
diagnosable. No key material is logged.

test_queue_server.py: pin the whole argv, asserting the System keychain
path is its own trailing argument after -w, and assert the not-found
error names the store searched. Verified non-vacuous: with the argv
change reverted the new test fails on the exact missing element.

DEPLOY.md:
- Step 1 needed a TTY it never asked for. The generate-and-store
  pipeline's sudo reads its password from the terminal, so on a cold
  timestamp it prompts mid-pipeline, and over the doc's own sanctioned
  non-interactive `ssh jvmbpro` path it fails outright ("a terminal is
  required to read the password") — JVMBPro has no NOPASSWD and no Touch
  ID for sudo. Split into 1a-1d, prime the timestamp with `sudo -v` as
  its own step, require an interactive terminal or `ssh -t`, and warn
  that a failed attempt must not be retried blindly because every run
  generates a different key.
- Step 1d certified a key the service cannot necessarily read. It ran
  find-generic-password WITHOUT -w while claiming to be "the same lookup
  shape the service itself performs". Without -w, security returns item
  ATTRIBUTES and never touches the item's data, so it performs no
  ACL/unlock authorization; queue_server.py reads WITH -w, which does. A
  GUI-prompting item — exactly the retired-v2-writer regression step 1a
  exists to catch — therefore prints "present" at 1d and then fails at
  service start under launchd, where there is no interactive
  authorization path, leaving the LaunchAgent throttle-looping while the
  runbook points back at a step that passed. Verified empirically on a
  locked temp keychain: the attribute-only lookup returned rc=0
  instantly, the identical lookup with -w blocked on an authorization
  prompt until killed. Add -w (the existing redirect still discards the
  value) and document that a hang here IS the failure.
- Step 2 could not run as written: it assumed queue_server.py and
  deploy/jvmbpro-delegate-queue/ existed in a JVMBPro checkout. JVMBPro's
  only checkout is ~/Documents/Code/ai-tools-mcp, which is the LIVE MCP
  server path (~/.claude.json runs uv run <that path>/mcp_server.py), so
  checking this branch out there would swap the running server. Replace
  with a push-from-the-Mini scp route into a staging dir, plus a
  throwaway-clone alternative, and state plainly that the live checkout
  must never be switched.
- The edge steps published the hostname before gating it. The old order
  was ingress -> proxied DNS CNAME -> create the Access application, and
  step 3 explicitly offered "add the hostname now and append the access
  block once the AUD tag exists". The service authenticates nothing
  itself (loopback callers are trusted by design; Access is the only
  remote gate), so between creating the CNAME and finishing the Access
  app anyone could POST /v1/jobs, run inference on JVMBPro, collect the
  result, and fill MAX_QUEUED=64 so Jason's own submits draw 429. The
  hostname is not obscure: it is hardcoded into _QUEUE_DEFAULT_CHAIN in
  this public repo. Reorder to Access application -> ingress carrying the
  real AUD tag -> proxied CNAME last, delete the append-later escape
  hatch so the ingress never lands ungated, and add a grey-cloud
  fallback for the case where the dashboard wants a record to exist.
- Step 5's token guidance was un-actionable AND over-shared. Keep the
  operational point (the ollama-mbp app's single non_identity policy
  includes FIVE service tokens and only one is the one the MCP client
  sends; picking another returns a bare 403) but identify it by matching
  against the local OLLAMA_CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_ID Keychain item's first
  eight characters. That is self-verifying on the machine instead of
  requiring a memorized id.
- Redact private Cloudflare infrastructure identifiers. This repo is
  public and none of these values were on origin/main; committing them
  would publish them permanently. Replaced with placeholders plus how to
  obtain each locally: tunnel UUID (cloudflared tunnel list), zone id (a
  zone-list call reusing the same Keychain-piped-token pattern), Zero
  Trust team name and AUD tag (dashboard). Dropped the service token's
  name and client-id entirely, and dropped the enumeration of the other
  live ingress hostnames on that tunnel — it advertised unrelated
  remote-access endpoints on Jason's laptop and the operator only needed
  "insert before the catch-all". ollama-mbp.djvassallo.com stays; it is
  pre-existing deliberate precedent (README.md).
- Re-verified the rest against JVMBPro read-only: uv at
  /opt/homebrew/bin/uv, port 11438 free, keychain-write is the v3 zsh
  wrapper, no DELEGATE_QUEUE_KEY item yet (rc 44), curl 8.7.1 (the -H @-
  claim), and no queue-mbp ingress. Fixed an `ssh jvmbpro ~/...` that
  expanded on the wrong host and corrected the step-6 healthz sample to
  the real response shape. No secret values are printed anywhere in the

NovelTea is a self-hosted, offline-first long-form writing app, Scrivener-shaped: a binder tree, document snapshots, labels/statuses, custom metadata, saved/smart collections, and compile presets. Clients are web, Tauri (Windows/macOS), and iOS. Every client keeps a full local replica and works fully disconnected.

- **`WireEnumTest`** drives off the enum constants themselves, so a new value is covered the moment it is added: round-tripping, unique lowercase wire forms, case and whitespace tolerance, and empty (never an exception) for null, blank, unknown and injection-shaped input.
- **`EnumSchemaAlignmentTest`** reads the allowed values out of `pg_constraint` and compares them to the enum, then writes every value to the real table. The enum and the CHECK constraint are two declarations of one fact in different languages; nothing but this keeps them honest. Add a value to one and not the other and it fails, naming the constraint.

## Compile

`packages/compile` turns ProseMirror documents into the formats Core ships (`txt`, `md`, `html`). `ExportProvider` on the Java side reports the same boundary; a commercial module contributes the remaining formats by supplying another implementation, and Core must keep working with only its own provider present.

### binder_item

The tree structure — folders, documents, trash. This is the Scrivener "binder."

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|

| type | enum | `folder` \| `document` \| `trash` |
| title | text | |
| order_index | float | fractional indexing — lets you reorder/insert without rewriting siblings *(superseded — see A4)* |
| icon | text, nullable | optional custom icon (Scrivener-style) |
| deleted_at | timestamptz, nullable | soft delete — needed for sync tombstones |
| version | bigint | monotonic, incremented on every change |
| updated_by_device_id | uuid | for conflict attribution |

| id | uuid | same as binder_item.id, or separate FK — recommend same id for simplicity |
| content | jsonb | ProseMirror doc JSON |
| word_count | int | derived, cached for fast binder display |
| synopsis | text, nullable | the Scrivener index-card text |
| notes | text, nullable | document notes (rich text or plain) |
| version | bigint | incremented per content save |
| updated_at | timestamptz | |

### snapshot

Manual or auto point-in-time captures of a document's content (Scrivener's snapshot feature).

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|

### label / status

Scrivener-style metadata taxonomies, per project.

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|

### custom_metadata_field + custom_metadata_value

For arbitrary caller-defined metadata (Scrivener's custom meta-data pane). Field defs at the project level, values keyed per binder_item.

### collection

- Each entity carries a version integer, bumped on every write.
- Client pushes a batch: {entity, base_version, new_data} for each locally-changed record since last sync.
- Server accepts if base_version matches current server version (no one else changed it since the client last knew about it). Otherwise it's a conflict.
- On conflict for document content: don't try to merge rich text — create a sibling binder_item titled "<original title> (Conflicted Copy, <device>, <timestamp>)" containing the client's version, and let the caller manually reconcile. This mirrors Dropbox/Scrivener's own

Allowlist link schemes, sweep every route for IDOR, drop product names

Fixes a real cross-site scripting hole in compiled output. Link hrefs were
escaped but their scheme was never checked, so a document containing
javascript:alert(1) produced a working anchor in every format that carries
links. Escaping cannot help there: the payload contains nothing that needs
escaping. isSafeHref now allowlists http, https, mailto and relative
references, normalising away case, whitespace and control characters first so
JaVaScRiPt: and an embedded tab do not slip past, and failing closed on schemes
nobody has listed. An unsafe link loses its anchor, keeps its text, and warns.
Markdown gets the same treatment, since markdown links execute in renderers.

IdorSweepTest enumerates every route from the handler mapping and drives each
one with a stranger's token. Routes naming another account's resource must not
answer 2xx; caller-scoped collections may, but must not contain the victim's
data; nothing may answer 500; and the victim's project must be unchanged
afterwards. Reading the mapping rather than a hand-written list means a new
controller method that forgets its authorization check fails immediately.

Removes third-party product names from tracked files, replacing them with
descriptions of the behaviour they referred to.

190 Java and 95 Node tests green. Verified by mutation: making the ownership
check pass for everyone turns the sweep red.

Add multi-tenant support: multiple restaurants, one system

Every restaurant's data is now isolated by a new Restaurant model —
tables, comandas, menu, orders, payments, coupons, help calls, audit
log and staff all carry a restaurantId and are scoped by it end to
end. This is the foundation for self-service onboarding ("reach the
market") and for a future iFood/delivery-platform channel to slot in
next to KIOSK/DELIVERY/SCHEDULED.

Architecture:
- New `Restaurant` model (id, slug, createdAt). `Settings` keyed by
  restaurantId instead of a hardcoded "singleton" row.
- QR tokens (table/comanda) and the Checkout id stay globally unique
  on purpose — that's how an anonymous QR scan resolves its own
  restaurant with no slug/login needed. Human-facing numbers (table
  number, comanda number, order number/pickup ticket, coupon code)
  become unique per restaurant instead of globally.
- User.email stays globally unique (keeps /login simple: no
  restaurant selection before the password prompt).
- Every by-id staff mutation (delete/update) now scopes on
  {id, restaurantId} via deleteMany/updateMany + a count check,
  instead of trusting a bare id — closes an IDOR class of bug that a
  single-tenant system never had to worry about.
- Realtime SSE topics ("kitchen"/"pdv") are now per-restaurant
  (`kitchen:${restaurantId}`) so one restaurant's live board never
  sees another's events.
- /totem and /pedir move to /totem/[slug] and /pedir/[slug] — the only
  public screens with no QR Code to resolve a restaurant from. New
  /signup does self-service onboarding (Restaurant + Settings + first
  ADMIN user, auto-login), also used as the isolation test's own
  second-tenant fixture.
- Data migration backfills all pre-existing rows onto one
  'rst_default' restaurant (slug "principal") — the real restaurant
  already in production, preserved verbatim.

Found and fixed during isolation testing: the order-number Counter
row wasn't migrated to its new per-restaurant key, so the first order
placed after the migration collided with an existing order number
(unique constraint violation). Added a small follow-up migration that
renames the counter key, preserving the existing sequence.

Verified: full TypeScript + lint clean, production build clean. A
12-point isolation test (via /signup, creating a real second
restaurant on an isolated DB copy) confirms: empty dashboards for a
new tenant, 404 on cross-tenant IDOR attempts by id, independent
per-restaurant numbering/coupons/audit log, SSE events never leaking
across restaurants, and /totem/[slug] serving only its own menu.
Separately reran the full real-restaurant regression (QR order → PDV
payment → totem → painel → reports) after the fix.

Fix Google Sign-In race condition on the OAuth callback page (#93)

* Fix AdSense low-value-content rejection: unblock exam content from crawlers

ExamDetailPage rendered a login-gated placeholder (identical hardcoded
stat boxes on every page) to anonymous visitors, which is what Googlebot
sees since the site is statically exported with no live session at build
time. 220 of 308 sitemap URLs were affected. Removed the auth gate so the
real per-exam Overview/Eligibility/Syllabus/Exam Pattern/Salary content
is publicly readable; bookmarking still independently prompts login via
its own isAuthenticated check.

Also removed /login, /register, and duplicate ?category= filter URLs
from sitemap.xml — they contradicted robots.txt and added no unique
content.

* Enable native push notifications and fix Google Sign-In for local builds

Firebase project is now configured (google-services.json obtained from
console) so the native push registration that was disabled after the
login-crash root-cause fix can be safely restored — PushNotifications
.register() no longer throws on missing FirebaseApp init.

- Commit google-services.json (no secret values; the API key is
  restricted by Android package name and ships inside every built APK
  regardless, so gitignoring it only bought inconsistent CI builds)
- Reinstall @capacitor/push-notifications, restore its config block and
  FCM token registration logic (registration/error/received/action
  listeners, permission request, register())
- Re-sync Android native project (5 plugins now, was 4)
- Add NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID to frontend/.env.production using the
  Web OAuth client Firebase auto-created for the Google sign-in provider,
  so local Windows builds get working Google Sign-In like CI builds
  already do via the REACT_APP_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID GitHub secret

* Fix Google Client ID mismatch: use the client already wired to backend

The Firebase-auto-created Web client (from google-services.json) is a
different OAuth client than the one backend/GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID on Render
actually expects — its default redirect URIs are Firebase's own auth
handler, not this app's /auth/google/callback. Swapped
NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID in .env.production to match Render's
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID so local Windows builds are consistent with backend.

* Fix Google Sign-In race condition: wait for router.isReady before reading code

Screen recording showed the OAuth flow reaching Google's account chooser
successfully (confirming the Client ID/redirect URI fix was correct), then
failing with "No authorization code received" immediately after redirect
back to /auth/google/callback.

Root cause: this page is statically exported, so next/router's router.query
starts empty and is only populated with the URL's query string after
client-side hydration parses it. The effect that reads searchParams.get
('code') ran on mount before that hydration completed, saw an empty query,
and gave up — even though the real code/state were in the URL the whole
time. This is exactly the path taken when Google redirects into the Chrome
Custom Tab opened from the native app (a genuine fresh page load, not an
in-app client-side transition), which is why it only showed up there.

Fix: guard the effect on router.isReady so it waits for hydration to finish
parsing the query string before deciding no code was received. Also fixed
the "no code" error branch to actually redirect to /login after 3s like its
sibling error branches do, instead of leaving the user on a dead-end screen.

+This document lists known duplicate security advisory clusters for [OliveTin/OliveTin](https://github.com/OliveTin/OliveTin). When triaging new reports, check here and [open advisories](https://github.com/OliveTin/OliveTin/security/advisories) before accepting.
+
+**Duplicate policy:** the earliest reporter on the canonical advisory receives primary credit. Later reporters are credited on the canonical advisory when closed as duplicates. See [SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md).
+
+## Triage checklist
+
+1. Search open advisories for the same component and attack path.
+2. Match against clusters below.
+3. If duplicate: close the newer advisory, link to canonical, add reporter to canonical credits.
+4. If unique: accept, patch on a private branch, reassess CVSS with OliveTin context (see SECURITY.md — OliveTin is intentional RCE by design).
+5. Merge fix to `next`, publish advisory, credit reporters in advisory body (not commit message).
+
+---
+
+## shellAfterCompleted command injection
+
+**Canonical:** [GHSA-vc6p-m6vx-6cwq](https://github.com/OliveTin/OliveTin/security/advisories/GHSA-vc6p-m6vx-6cwq) — reporter **knight-yagami** (2026-03-04)
+
+Untrusted command output or template variables interpolated into `shellAfterCompleted` and executed via `sh -c`.
+
+| GHSA | Reporter | Status | Notes |
+|------|----------|--------|-------|
+| GHSA-vc6p-m6vx-6cwq | knight-yagami | closed (canonical) | Original report |
+| GHSA-v5gc-hqpq-227p | 0xkakash1 | closed (duplicate) | Output template variant |
+| GHSA-m7wr-wj5j-7459 | Ryu7zz | duplicate | Webhook `exec` → output → `shellAfterCompleted` |
+| GHSA-cjxm-x848-6vmc | Yesuhei | duplicate | Missing shell safety on after-completion |
+| GHSA-j9p9-36jc-2v8w | anushkavirgaonkar | duplicate | Same root cause |
+
+**Fix:** shell-quote `output`/`exitCode` before template render; block `shellAfterCompleted` for webhook-tagged actions.
+
+**CVSS note:** requires admin-configured `shellAfterCompleted` and attacker influence on output — typically PR:H not PR:N.
+
+---
+
+## OAuth2 state map memory exhaustion (DoS)
+
+**Canonical:** [GHSA-xpxj-f2fm-rqch](https://github.com/OliveTin/OliveTin/security/advisories/GHSA-xpxj-f2fm-rqch) — reporter **knight-yagami** (2026-03-04)
+
+Unauthenticated `/oauth/login` grows `registeredStates` without TTL or cap.
+
+| GHSA | Reporter | Status | Notes |
+|------|----------|--------|-------|
+| GHSA-xpxj-f2fm-rqch | knight-yagami | closed (canonical) | Original report |
+| GHSA-cj96-c55v-2f3c | Dredsen | duplicate | Same unbounded map |

+**Fix:** TTL sweep (match 15-minute cookie MaxAge), max map size, cleanup on failed callback.
+
+**CVSS note:** unauthenticated DoS — reported 7.5 is appropriate.

RECUPERACAO DE TRABALHO PERDIDO.

O commit eaea83b (VPS, 16/08 22:34 UTC) foi apagado do main por um
`git push -f`. Este merge o traz de volta.

Como aconteceu: o pull desta maquina foi em 09/08 17:55, trazendo aca9ffa.
A VPS commitou eaea83b UMA SEMANA DEPOIS, em 16/08. O branch local nunca
soube dele; o push foi recusado por historico divergente e o -f mandou
sobrescrever. Os dois ramos partiam da mesma base (aca9ffa).

O QUE VOLTOU (62 arquivos)
- SQL injection corrigido em SendMail.ts e queues.ts (arquivos DIFERENTES
  dos que a auditoria daqui corrigiu — as duas se complementam)
- sequelize 5.22.5 -> 6.37.8, sequelize-typescript 1.1.0 -> 2.1.6,
  sequelize-cli 5.5.1 -> 6.6.5, com 77 erros de tipo corrigidos e bugs
  reais expostos pela tipagem estrita (guard morto em timeUseBotQueues,
  paginacao de Tags/ContactLists, campos fantasma em .update())
- ~10 dependencias com CVE: axios 1.7.9 -> 1.19.0 (~15 CVEs), jsonwebtoken
  8.5.1 -> 9.0.3, multer, nodemailer, puppeteer, baileys rc9 -> rc14
- bcrypt de custo 8 para 12
- SSH endurecido, fail2ban, ufw; backups com umask 077
- CSP + Permissions-Policy no nginx do frontend
- nginx/sites/crm.conf passa a ser versionado

RESOLUCAO DOS CONFLITOS (2 arquivos, ambos de dependencia)

O git juntou `server_tokens off;` dos DOIS lados em nginx.conf. Diretiva
duplicada no mesmo contexto faz o nginx recusar a config inteira e nao
subir — teria derrubado o site no deploy. Duplicata removida e validado
com `nginx -t` em container: syntax is ok.

VERIFICACAO
- npm ci com lockfile mesclado: 1109 pacotes, limpo
- tsc --noEmit: limpo (o modulo de tokens escrito contra sequelize 5 e

LICAO REGISTRADA
Nunca usar `git push -f` neste repositorio. Com commits vindo desta
maquina e da VPS, force push apaga trabalho de quem commitou por ultimo.

def _get_store() -> rag.VectorStore:
    global _store
    if _store is None:
        _store = rag.VectorStore.load()
    return _store

def handle(message: str, trace: Trace) -> str:
    hits = _get_store().search(message, k=3)
    relevant = [h for h in hits if h.score >= rag.RELEVANCE_FLOOR]

    if not relevant:
        # Grounding guarantee: no relevant doc -> abstain, don't invent.
        raise AbstainError("no knowledge-base match above relevance floor")

    context = "\n\n".join(f"[{h.doc.source}] {h.doc.text}" for h in relevant)

fix(security): AuthPrincipal.userId ở certificates/grading + chặn quyền rỗng

Lỗi có sẵn từ P5, phát hiện khi verify P7 (KHÔNG do P7 gây ra).

Gốc: `@CurrentUser()` trả `AuthPrincipal { userId }`, nhưng certificates.service.ts và
grading.service.ts khai kiểu `AuthUser` rồi đọc `currentUser.id` / `currentUser.roles`
→ luôn undefined lúc chạy. Hậu quả đã xác nhận trên DB dev:

- `getEffectivePermissions(undefined)` → `userRole.findMany({ where: { userId: undefined } })`
  — Prisma coi undefined là "không lọc" → trả MỌI user_role → hợp nhất quyền của mọi role
  ≈ super_admin. Mọi kiểm quyền trong certificates đều pass.
- `listMine` lọc `userId: undefined` → trả chứng chỉ của MỌI học viên.
- `POST /certificates/:id/revoke` và `GET /certificates/:id/pdf` (chỉ JwtAuthGuard, scope
  kiểm trong service) → user bất kỳ thu hồi / tải được chứng chỉ người khác.
- `GET /classes/:classId/my-gradebook` ném 500 PrismaClientValidationError.

Sửa:
- certificates + grading nhận `AuthPrincipal` và dùng `currentUser.userId`. Bỏ shortcut
  `currentUser.roles?.includes('admin')` — admin/super_admin nhận quyền ở phạm vi GLOBAL
  nên `hasPermission` đã phủ (đối chiếu seed: cả hai có certificate.*/grade.read).
- `RbacService.getEffectivePermissions` trả quyền RỖNG khi userId falsy, không chạm DB —
  phòng thủ chiều sâu để một chỗ gọi sai không bao giờ thành cấp quyền toàn hệ thống.
- Test hồi quy (+6): rbac userId rỗng (undefined/null/''), revoke 403 + tra đúng userId,
  listMine lọc đúng userId, getPdfBuffer IDOR 403.

Verify: `pnpm validate` 16/16, api 180 test. Live sau vá: my-gradebook 200; HV không sở hữu
`/certificates/mine` = 0 (chủ sở hữu = 1), `:id/pdf` 403, `:id/revoke` 403; GV vẫn đọc được
`/certificates/class/:id` và `/gradebook` (200).

Ghi nhận nợ MỚI (chưa vá, có từ P6/D1): sinh PDF chứng chỉ 500 với tiếng Việt —
`WinAnsi cannot encode "ơ"` do pdf-lib StandardFonts; cần nhúng font Unicode qua fontkit.

feat(sales): ticket priority — pick on create, change after filing

Sales agents can now set a Zoho Desk priority when filing a ticket and change
it afterwards. Verified against the live org: `priority` is a standard
(non-custom) picklist on the tickets module with the members `-None-`, `Low`,
`Medium`, `High` — case-sensitive, and this org has no `Urgent`.

Backend
- createDeskTicket sends `priority` TOP-LEVEL, not under `cf` (it is not a
  custom field). Omitted when the agent leaves it at None.
- New `PATCH /v1/desk/tickets/:id/priority` → Desk `PATCH /tickets/{id}`.
  Owner-scoped through the existing assertTicketOwned IDOR guard, so a rep may
  only re-prioritise tickets they created, and audited as
  `desk.ticket.priority.update`.
- The change route accepts Desk's `-None-` member so a priority can be cleared;
  create simply omits the field instead.

Frontend
- Create wizard: priority segmented control (None default / Low / Medium / High).
- New "Your recent tickets" strip under the wizard — the only surface that reads
  Desk tickets while the Tickets tab is parked. Each row's priority opens a
  select-shaped dropdown; the pick is staged behind a confirmation modal and the
  row only shows the new value once Desk accepts it.

Timeout fix
- The Desk token has no `Desk.search.READ` scope, so the ticket list falls back

Fix Engage Series Publication and Access

Access to series and series metadata on the search service (shown in
media module and player) depends on the events published which are part
of the series. Publishing an event will automatically publish a series
and update access to it. Removing an event or republishing the event
should do the same.

Incorrectly Hiding Public Series
--------------------------------

This patch fixes the access control update to the series when a new
episode is being published. Until now, a new episode publication would
always update the series access with the episode access.

While this is no security issue since it can only cause the access to be
stricter, it may cause public series to become private. This would
happen, for example, if a users sets one episode of a series to private
and republishes the episode.

Now, the search service will merge the access control lists of all
episodes to grant access based on their combined access rules.

Update Series on Removal
------------------------

This patch fixes Opencast not updating the series access or remove a
published series if an event is being removed.

This means that access to a series is re-calculated when an episode is
being deleted based on the remaining published episodes in the series.
For example, removing the last episode with public access will now make
the series private which it would have stayed public before.

It also means that if the last episode of a series is being removed, the
series itself will be unpublished as well, so no empty series will
continue to show up any longer.

## Auth & roles
Login is by **email**, not username — the app has a `User` collection (`email`, `password`, `phone`,
`roleId`) and a separate `Role` collection (`name`, `description`, `isActive`). Role names are
user-manageable via the `/roles` screen; only the seeded `super_admin` role (constant in
`lib/constants/roles.ts`, never a raw string) is protected from rename/delete/deactivation.
`/roles` and `/users` are gated two ways: `components/Layout/Sidebar.tsx` hides the nav items unless
`useCurrentUser()`'s `role` equals `ROLES.SUPER_ADMIN` (cosmetic only), and every `/api/roles/**` +
`/api/users/**` route re-checks the role **fresh from the database** via `requireSuperAdmin()` in
`lib/requireAuth.ts` — never trust the JWT claim alone for this check, since a role can be changed or
deactivated after a token was issued.

def _decode_identity_bytes(raw: Any) -> tuple[str, bool]:
    """Decode an FC43 object defensively. Returns (text, decoded_cleanly).

    UTF-8 is tried FIRST, not ASCII. A Chinese, Japanese or German vendor name is
    ordinary in this market — 汇川, 三菱, Müller — and an ASCII-first decoder marks
    every one of them "not clean", which puts a corruption warning on a perfectly
    good asset register row and teaches the reader to ignore the flag. Only bytes
    that are genuinely not UTF-8 fall back to latin-1, and only those are flagged:
    latin-1 never raises, so it can silently mis-render, and the operator should
    know which fields might be wrong.
    """
    if isinstance(raw, list | tuple):
        parts = [_decode_identity_bytes(item) for item in raw]
        return " ".join(p[0] for p in parts if p[0]), all(p[1] for p in parts)
    if isinstance(raw, bytes | bytearray):
        try:
            return bytes(raw).decode("utf-8").strip("\x00 \t\r\n"), True
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            # latin-1 maps every byte, so this always yields something readable —
            # possibly wrongly, which is exactly why it is reported.
            return bytes(raw).decode("latin-1").strip("\x00 \t\r\n"), False
    return str(raw).strip(), True

async def security_headers(request: Request, call_next):
    # The frontend (Next.js) already sends these via next.config.js, but
    # the API itself sent none -- meaning /docs and /redoc (interactive,
    # unauthenticated-to-view API documentation, both HTML) had no
    # clickjacking protection, and no response from this service carried
    # any of these headers at all. security.tsx's own copy claims these
    # apply to "every response" -- this makes that actually true instead
    # of only true for the frontend half of the stack. Found in a security audit.
    response = await call_next(request)
    response.headers["X-Frame-Options"] = "DENY"
    response.headers["X-Content-Type-Options"] = "nosniff"
    response.headers["Referrer-Policy"] = "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"
    response.headers["Permissions-Policy"] = "camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()"
    return response

fix(oauth)!: require informed consent before issuing authorization codes

A successful Homebox login on /oauth/authorize was treated as consent, and the
page showed nothing about the requesting client. Combined with open dynamic
client registration, a crafted authorize link for an attacker-registered
redirect URI could obtain delegated access to a user's Homebox account without
the user ever seeing which application they authorized.

- Render a consent screen naming the client (client-declared, marked
  unverified), the host that will receive the code, the requested scope, the
  MCP resource and the client ID. POST /oauth/authorize now requires
  action=allow; action=deny redirects back with error=access_denied without
  using the submitted credentials, and a missing decision re-renders the page.
- Serve the page with Content-Security-Policy (default-src 'none', hashed
  inline stylesheet, form-action 'self' <redirect-origin>, base-uri 'none',
  frame-ancestors 'none'), Referrer-Policy, X-Frame-Options, nosniff and
  Cache-Control: no-store.
- Add the opt-in HOMEBOX_MCP_OAUTH_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_ORIGINS allowlist,
  enforced both at dynamic registration and at authorization so tightening it
  invalidates clients already persisted in oauth-store.json.

BREAKING CHANGE: POST /oauth/authorize requires action=allow. Browser-driven
connectors are unaffected.

## Development vs. evaluation

```text
corpus/
├── development/   public, tunable, regression-only — never a headline metric
└── evaluation/    the blind holdout — the only tier a headline metric can come from
```

This split exists for one reason: **the moment a fixture is used to diagnose
or fix a scanner bug, it stops measuring generalization and starts measuring
"did we regress on a known case."** Both are useful, but conflating them is
how a benchmark quietly turns into a training set its own maintainer is
unknowingly optimizing against.

The rule, mechanically enforced by `run_benchmark.py` (`validate_tier_matches_dir`)
and by policy for everything the tooling can't check automatically:

> **A fixture that has ever been used to diagnose, reproduce, or fix a
> scanner bug belongs in `development/` permanently. It must never move to
> `evaluation/`, regardless of how old the bug or how thoroughly it's since
> been fixed.**

The 12 fixtures this benchmark launched with already found two real skil
false positives (issues #33, #34) — which is exactly why all 12 are
classified `tier: development` and always will be, even after those issues
are fixed and the fixtures become permanent regression tests. `evaluation/`
starts empty. Filling it requires fixtures nobody has used to tune anything
against, which in practice means writing them somewhat independently of
active bug-fixing work, or asking someone who isn't fixing skil's bugs to
contribute them.

## Review status

Every fixture starts at `review.status: provisional`. A fixture only
becomes `gold` after **at least two independent human reviewers** agree
with its `ground_truth` and `rationale`. `run_benchmark.py` computes three
numbers per tool:

- **headline_metric** — `tier: evaluation` AND `review.status: gold` only.
  This is the only number meant to be quoted anywhere (README, `COMPARISON.md`,
  external claims). As of this benchmark's initial version, `evaluation/` is
  empty, so the headline metric correctly reads `"n/a"` for every tool.
  That's the runner working as designed, not a bug.
- **development_set_metric_regression_only_never_a_generalization_claim** —
  every `development/` fixture, regardless of review status. Use this to
  check for regressions after a fix; never cite it as evidence of detection
  quality.
- **evaluation_set_provisional_metric_informational_only** — `evaluation/`
  fixtures not yet at `gold`. Useful for iterating on new holdout fixtures
  before they're reviewed; also not a headline number.

If you review a fixture, open a PR changing its `review.status` to `gold`
and adding yourself to `review.reviewers` (a second reviewer approves by

## Extending the corpus

See `schema/fixture-v1.schema.json` for the fixture format and
`corpus/development/bench-001-instruction-override/` for a complete
example. A new fixture PR should include both the artifact, a `rationale` a
reviewer who has never seen skil's or the reference tool's source code
could still evaluate, and a `tier` matching which directory it lives in.
New fixtures not tied to a specific bug diagnosis should generally start
directly in `evaluation/` (still `provisional` until reviewed) rather than
`development/`, so the holdout set actually grows.

feat(eval): grade the tenant's own model — and fix the case source that never fired (#1264)

* feat(cloudagent): Stage 1 live discovery — confirm a flag against the account, not the snapshot

The AI Cloud Security Engineer reasoned entirely over a snapshot captured before it
started. That is fine for structure (an ARN does not move) but not for the flags a path
actually turns on — a security group left open, a role still holding admin. Those change,
and a stale snapshot is wrong in BOTH directions: a path reported live may already be
closed, and one dismissed as closed may have re-opened. Neither was detectable.

get_resource(id, live:true) now re-reads that resource from the account and answers
AGREES / DIFFERS / COULD NOT CHECK against the snapshot.

The safety envelope was already built and tested — it was simply never reachable. This
wires it: awsfetch's read-only listers (already used by inventory sync) behind an SDK-free
cloudagent.LiveReader, so cloudagent keeps the AWS SDK out of it the same way the
*remediate packages do. Read-only by construction — awsfetch issues only describe/list
verbs and the role is assumed with cloudsafety.SessionPolicy(), which denies mutation
outright, so this cannot become a write path.

The load-bearing distinction is COULD NOT CHECK. An id on a surface that was skipped comes
back not-covered with the reason — never not-found, which the agent would correctly read as
"it was deleted". Concluding a bucket is gone because an API call was never made would drop
a real attack path on the strength of a call that never happened, so awsfetch's existing
Covers()/Coverage() honesty carries all the way into the agent's observation.

It rides on get_resource rather than taking a 13th catalog slot: the ≤12 cap is enforced by
TestToolCatalogStaysWithinTheCap and exists because tool-use accuracy degrades past ~12 —
the same reason estate_context is one tool and not three. (I tried it as its own tool first;
that test caught it.) Appending also puts the graph view and the live view in ONE
observation, so the agent compares them directly.

The account is read ONCE per investigation and cached, so N questions cost one read — what
makes the capability affordable enough to leave enabled. Nil reader (no fetcher wired, or no
connected account) is a real answer: the snapshot is UNCONFIRMED, never "current".

Tested: unread-surface-is-not-absence, read-surface-absence-is-a-deletion, drift detection,
unconfigured/error honesty, reachability through the live flag, and single-read caching.
Mutation-verified (treating an unread surface as covered compiles and fails the test).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(runner): run L1.5 on the ENGINE scan path — the product's primary path skipped it

Researching whether a human security engineer can actually use this product surfaced a
defect far bigger than the UI gaps I went looking for.

The L1.5 chain (§11) did NOT run on platform engine scans. Only cmd/tsengine (the CLI)
ever constructed a tracer; there is none in internal/orchestrator or internal/sandbox, and
runner.scanAsset took what the scanner returned and called PutFinding directly. So every
repo, container, web, api and ip scan through the PRODUCT stored findings with:

  - no KEV listing and no EPSS score (the exploited-in-the-wild and patch-priority signals)
  - no exploitability or surface_priority
  - no FP filtering
  - no compliance mapping
  - no corroboration, confidence or verification_status

Meanwhile ~15 secondary ingest paths all call enrichFindings("L1.5 parity §11"). The
asymmetry ran OPPOSITE to what every comment claimed — including enrichFindings' own doc,
which asserted engine findings "already get this via the sandbox tracer", and CLAUDE.md §11,
which said the hooks fire on them "by construction". Both are corrected here.

This is precisely what makes or breaks the audience in question. Practitioners prioritise by
exploited-in-the-wild and triage by confidence; a list with neither is the raw scanner noise
the market says costs more than it saves (organisations willing to rely on AI pentesting fell
to 9% in 2026 from 29%, and 78% report critical false negatives).

Extracts the chain to internal/l15 — its own package because platformapi imports runner (so
runner cannot import back) and it cannot live in internal/tracer (hooks already imports
tracer). platformapi.enrichFindings stays as a thin wrapper so the ingest call sites are
untouched. Also enriches the runner's OWN sync paths (GitHub-org SSPM, OSINT), which were
asymmetric with their HTTP twins for the identical assessor.

Tested on consequence rather than plumbing: a stored engine finding must carry
verification_status + confidence, and TSENGINE_L15_DISABLED must still yield a raw finding
so the §14.1 ablation stays measurable. Mutation-verified; full tree green by exit code.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(platform): expose what L1.5 suppressed — the security engineer's audit surface

Second half of making this usable by a human security engineer. The first fixed the
enrichment not running at all; this makes its DECISIONS auditable.

CLAUDE.md §2.5 requires L1.5 demotions and dismissals to be "logged + recoverable so the
L1 audience can audit them", and §2.1 frames that audience as a peer, not a subordinate.
The engine has always honoured it — vulnerabilities.json carries l15_audit_log — but the
PRODUCT never exposed it. A security engineer on the platform could see what the AI chose
to show them and not what it chose to hide, which is the precise affordance practitioners
say they need before trusting a tool: not "is it right" but "let me check where it wasn't".

The gap is narrower than it first looks, and that shaped the design. A SURVIVING finding
already carries its own RawOutput and ToolArgs, so what the tool said is recoverable. What
is not recoverable is a finding the FP filter DISMISSED — it appears in no findings list,
no issue, no incident — or one it DEMOTED, which shows only its new severity. So the audit
trail, not a raw-findings mirror, is the thing that had to be persisted.

- l15.EnrichDetailed returns the trail alongside the enriched set (Enrich unchanged).
- Engagement.L15Audit persists it, following the ToolsRan/ToolsFailed precedent.
- GET /v1/l15-audit aggregates it: entries, dropped vs demoted counts, and a per-rule
  roll-up sorted noisiest-first — one filter rule quietly suppressing forty findings is
  the decision an engineer is most likely to want to argue with, and it is invisible until
  aggregated by rule.

Grounded (§10): an empty trail over a scanned estate returns an explicit note that scans
predating the trail (or run with L1.5 disabled) record nothing, and that this is NOT
evidence nothing was suppressed — the same discipline as coverage and posture.

Tested end to end: a REAL scan through runner.scanAsset records the trail on its engagement
(2 entries from a decoy fixture), so the surface is populated in production rather than only
by tests. Tree green by explicit exit code 0.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(platform): POST /v1/replay — the security engineer's dig-deeper, on the product

Third security-engineer gap. §9 describes tool-replay as "the dig-deeper capability
webappsec exposes to security engineers", and it has existed since Phase 5 — mounted only
on the ENGINE CLI's server. The product's users, the ones with an actual queue to work
through, could only accept or reject what the AI chose to run.

That is the affordance the market research puts at the centre: practitioners trust AI
output only as far as they can verify it, and verification means re-running the thing
yourself with your own arguments — nuclei with my template, sqlmap with a tamper script.

Deliberately NOT a reuse of internal/replay.Replay: that loads the original scan from a
runs DIRECTORY to recover its pinned corpus, and the platform keeps scans in the store, not
on disk. What is shared is the contract — a replay finding is stamped
DiscoveryMethod{tool_replay, replayOf} so it can never be mistaken for something a scheduled
scan discovered.

- runner.ToolReplayer: optional interface, exactly like ReportingScanRunner, because the
  operate path assesses a posted snapshot and has no tools to re-run. A scanner that cannot
  replay returns 503 with the reason rather than an empty 200 that reads as "ran, found
  nothing".
- EngineRunner.ReplayTool spawns the sandbox, dispatches ONE tool, and lets the engineer's
  args (including a target override, which §9 permits) win over the defaults.
- Replay findings run the same L1.5 chain as everything else, so the answer is comparable
  with the rest of the queue.
- store:false by default — a replay is an INVESTIGATION, and most should not permanently
  enlarge the queue the engineer is trying to shrink.
- An empty replay says it is a result about THOSE arguments and does not clear the target,
  the same grounding as coverage and the audit surface.

Tenant scoping is the load-bearing part and is tested as such: replay aims a scanner at a
target, so resolving an asset by id alone would let one tenant point the engine at another's
infrastructure. Mutation-verified — bypassing the scope compiles and the test catches it
scanning the other tenant's host. Tree green by explicit exit code 0.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(platform): reinstate a suppressed finding — the override half of §2.5

Visibility without override is half an affordance. Telling a security engineer "rule X
dropped 40 findings" while giving them no way to disagree leaves the AI's judgement final,
which is the posture practitioners explicitly reject. §2.5 is unambiguous that the audit
log is exposed to the security engineer "for override", not just for reading.

I had assumed a dismissed finding was unrecoverable. It is not: tracer.Add records t.raw
BEFORE the hooks run, so the dropped finding survives in the tracer — the platform simply
never persisted it. That makes override a small change rather than a redesign, and it
refines the earlier insight: not every raw finding (a survivor already carries its own
RawOutput and ToolArgs, and a MERGED finding is represented by the survivor it folded
into), but precisely the DISMISSED ones, which are the single case with nothing left behind.

- l15.Result.Dismissed recovers the dropped findings by matching the ids the chain recorded

The pentester's half of "dig deeper". An engineer looks at an unproven lead, believes the

finding UNCONDITIONALLY (an un-demonstrated lead comes back "unchanged", not nil). Treating

* feat(eval): regression over time, with a hard refusal to compare what is not comparable

The point-in-time score could not answer the question that actually differentiates this —
"is the agent getting worse on MY estate?" — which no public benchmark can answer at all.
It also happens to be the easiest place in the product to lie by accident, because two
percentages will subtract whether or not they measure the same thing.

Two rules, both of which refuse to draw a line rather than draw a misleading one:

  1. One sample is not a trend. Rendering a single run as flat implies a stability nobody
     observed.
  2. A trend across a CHANGING case set is not comparable. The suite grows every time
     someone reinstates a finding or marks one a false positive — exactly the behaviour we
     want — but 80% of ten cases and 80% of twelve are different measurements, and
     comparing them would punish a customer for grading more of their own estate.

SuiteHash makes rule 2 enforceable rather than aspirational: it fingerprints the graded set
INCLUDING each expectation, so a reversed judgement (suppressed, then reinstated) also
breaks comparability even though membership did not change.

that Postgres existed via the `var _ Store` assertion, and it needed ORDER BY seq rather
than the rowid the SQLite path uses. Runs are recorded only when there are graded cases: an
empty suite has no score, so persisting it would put meaningless points on a timeline. The
handler sorts by RanAt rather than trusting store ordering, since TrendOf compares the last
two and the four backends order by different columns.

Fixes a real cross-site scripting hole in compiled output. Link hrefs were
escaped but their scheme was never checked, so a document containing
javascript:alert(1) produced a working anchor in every format that carries
links. Escaping cannot help there: the payload contains nothing that needs
escaping. isSafeHref now allowlists http, https, mailto and relative
references, normalising away case, whitespace and control characters first so
JaVaScRiPt: and an embedded tab do not slip past, and failing closed on schemes
nobody has listed. An unsafe link loses its anchor, keeps its text, and warns.
Markdown gets the same treatment, since markdown links execute in renderers.

1.9.3 - `unreleased`

- Fixed arbitrary certificate revocation at the CA (`GHSA-pxmc-2ffp-8j67`_). Certificate identity was tracked
  only by Lemur's internal database row, not by the actual CA-side certificate. Any authenticated caller could
  upload a duplicate record for a certificate they didn't own (matching an existing ``authority_id`` and
  ``serial``) and then revoke it via ``PUT /api/1/certificates/<id>/revoke``, causing the CA to revoke the
  real certificate belonging to another caller. ``POST /api/1/certificates/upload`` now requires
  ``AuthorityPermission`` on the specified authority, and rejects uploads whose ``(authority_id, serial)``

fix(intelligence): fix IDOR on generation failure and feedback endpoints

Both GET /intelligence/generations/{generation_id}/failure and
POST /intelligence/feedback accessed or created data based on a
generation_id from the request body/path without verifying that
the generation's parent project belongs to the current user.

Added ownership checks: look up the Generation, then verify
project ownership via ProjectRepository.get_by_id(project_id, user_id).

Fixes 2 CONFIRMED IDORs per IDOR_AUDIT_REPORT.md.

fix(console): the checkout spec sends the Idempotency-Key its client always sends (AGL-2163)

A stale fixture, NOT a money-path defect — checked first, because the red
looked like one. The Billing page mints a key per attempt and sends
`Idempotency-Key` on every `/api/billing/checkout` call
(`app/(app)/[orgSlug]/billing/page.tsx`), and the route consumes it into
`claimAttempt`. Both halves are correct and it is the only caller. The
console checkout is protected.

What was wrong is that this spec could not have told the difference. Its
hand-written `pluginRequestFromWeb` forwarded three headers BY NAME —
`authorization`, `origin`, `host` — so the route's
`headers['idempotency-key']` was always empty no matter what the fixture
sent. Another closed-world mock, this one blinding a money-path suite to
the exact property AGL-2163 is about. When AGL-2163 made the keyless
branch `console.warn` that it is an unprotected money call, this spec's
blanket `expect(warnings).toHaveLength(0)` — there to catch a MISSING
metered item — caught its own unfaithful request instead.

So: the real `pluginRequestFromWeb` via `requireActual` (it is pure — no
Next internals), with `origin`/`host` layered UNDER the real headers
because the platform adds them and a bare Web `Request` cannot; a request
that carries the key; and an `apiIdempotency` store double that models
the one Firestore behaviour the claim is built on — `create()` REJECTS on
an existing document, which is the whole dedupe primitive. A double that
resolved instead would fabricate a green for a route that double-charges.
One key per call, because one call here is one attempt: a shared key
would make the second call a REPLAY, which never reaches Stripe, leaving
every assertion checking a stale `capturedBody`.

Forced red, twice. Dropping the `Idempotency-Key` header: 3 failed, the
UNPROTECTED-money-call warning back on every attempt. Pointing
`STRIPE_PRICE_METERED_YEARLY` at the monthly id: 2 failed, including
"NEVER puts the monthly metered price on an annual subscription" — the
mixed-interval assertion Stripe rejects outright. The guard still bites.

Friendship requests implementation (#10)

* chore(context): promote friendship-requests + PRD/roadmap to project-level context

friendship-requests will need frontend phases; backend/context/ was
backend-only. Moved friendship-requests, prd.md, roadmap.md,
shape-notes.md from backend/context/ to root context/ (already the
project-wide source of truth per stack-assessment.md/health-check.md,
both re-run at root on 2026-07-27). backend/context/ keeps its
backend-only archive (api-exception-handling, admin-load, etc.) per
explicit decision. Fixed api-exception-handling references to point at
its backend/context/archive/ location, and corrected roadmap.md's stale
"frontend is a separate repo" baseline note.

* feat(friendship-requests): friendship data model (p1)

Entity, enum, migration, repository, and fixtures for the Friendship
domain: FriendRequest (requester/addressee ManyToOne, status enum
incl. CANCELLED for future cancel support, createdAt/respondedAt),
partial unique index guaranteeing at most one active (pending/
accepted) pair regardless of direction, self-request CHECK constraint.
Deterministic fixtures cover accepted/pending/cooldown-active/
cooldown-expired states.

Also lands the planning-session updates to context/changes/
friendship-requests/{change,plan,plan-brief,research}.md (full-stack
promotion + 6-phase plan).

* feat(friendship-requests): friendship service layer (p2)

FriendshipService with sendRequest/acceptRequest/declineRequest/
cancelRequest/listFriends/listPending, seven domain exceptions
implementing ApiExceptionInterface, explicit symfony/clock dependency,
FRIEND_REQUEST_COOLDOWN_DAYS env config (added to .env.test; .env
itself is sandbox-restricted, see run notes for the required manual
follow-up). Cancel deliberately exempt from the decline cooldown.
15 new FriendshipServiceTest cases cover every business rule
including the check-ordering edge cases.

* feat(friendship-requests): friendship HTTP layer & tests (p3)

FriendshipController (send/list-pending/accept/decline/cancel/
list-friends), FriendshipVoter (addressee-only accept/decline,
requester-only cancel, no admin bypass), SendFriendRequestDto,
FriendRequestDto response mapper. Controller manually resolves
FriendRequest via repository (not #[MapEntity]) so a missing id
returns the specific FRIEND_REQUEST_NOT_FOUND code instead of a
generic one. 14 new FriendshipControllerTest cases cover the full
HTTP surface including authorization and duplicate/cooldown/
already-friends error paths.

* feat(friendship-requests): user search endpoint (p4)

New GET /users search action on the existing non-admin UserController
(not Admin\UserController), open to any authenticated user via the
access_control catch-all. Trimmed UserSearchResultDto (id/name/email/
avatar, no roles/status). UserRepository gains excludeUserId on
findWithPagination/countWithFilters, additive and defaulted to null
so the existing admin search is unaffected. Blank/missing search
returns an empty list rather than the full user table. 6 new
UserControllerTest cases; existing Admin\UserControllerTest coverage
verified unchanged.

* feat(friendship-requests): friendship data layer (p5, frontend)

types/friends.ts (FriendRequestsResponse deliberately breaks from the
{data: T[]} convention to match the backend's actual incoming/outgoing
shape). lib/apiErrors.ts::getApiErrorMessage() - the first instance in
this codebase of mapping the backend's error code to a specific
user-facing message instead of a generic toast. Six hooks (useFriends,
useFriendRequests, useSendFriendRequest, useAcceptFriendRequest,
useDeclineFriendRequest, useCancelFriendRequest,
useSearchFriendCandidates) following the existing
useGroupMembers/useAddGroupMember templates. 8 hook tests covering
success + at least one mapped-error case per mutation.

* feat(friendship-requests): friendship UI wiring (p6, frontend)

Wired the previously mock-only FriendsView.tsx to the real hooks:
useFriends/useFriendRequests replace MOCK_*, Accept/Decline/Cancel
buttons call the Phase 5 mutation hooks, loading skeleton added.
Removed the Suggestions tab entirely (no backend support) and the
mutualEvents field/stat (no backend source, not faked). "Wyślij
wiadomość" and "Usuń ze znajomych" render visibly disabled (no
messaging feature exists; unfriend is explicitly parked) via
title-attribute tooltips rather than the shadcn Tooltip primitive,
since Radix's disabled state sets pointer-events:none and would
suppress a hover-based tooltip anyway. New SendFriendRequestDialog
(search-as-you-type over GET /users, replacing the inert header
button). Sidebar's Friends nav badge now reflects the live incoming
pending-request count instead of a hardcoded 0.

* chore(friendship-requests): close out plan (epilogue)

Write back final phase SHA into Progress; change.md status -> implemented.
Every #### Automated row across all 6 phases is checked; the 9
remaining #### Manual rows (1.4, 3.3, 3.4, 4.3, 6.5-6.9) are pending
human verification per the run report.

* fix(friendship): harden concurrent send race and fix request-id IDOR leak

Catch the DB-level unique-constraint violation when two sendRequest
calls race past the app-level active-pair check, translating it into
a clean 409 instead of a raw 500. Non-participants attempting
accept/decline/cancel on a request id now get 404 instead of 403, so
they can no longer distinguish "exists" from "doesn't exist" via the
status code.

Also sets MAILER_DSN=null://null in the test env so functional tests
stop sending real mail through the dev Mailpit instance.

* fix(friends): use native disabled prop on parked dropdown menu items

"Wyślij wiadomość" and "Usuń ze znajomych" only looked disabled via
manual opacity/cursor classes — pointer-events stayed enabled and
aria-disabled was never set, so the items were still clickable and
screen readers didn't announce them as disabled. Switching to
DropdownMenuItem's disabled prop (plus the destructive variant for
unfriend) uses the primitive's own data-[disabled] styling instead.

* impl_review(friendship-requests): fix findings from implementation review

Resolved critical and warning findings from the Friendship Requests implementation review:
- Fixed concurrent sendRequest race causing raw 500 instead of clean 409.
- Added missing HTTP-layer tests for request states and cooldown expiry.
- Unified non-participant request actions to return 404 (vs. 403).
Updated implementation plan status to `impl_reviewed`.

* chore(archive): close friendship-requests

* style(friends): run prettier over friendship-requests files, fix CI format:check

Frontend CI's format:check job failed on 11 files from the earlier
Phase 5/6 friendship-requests commits that were never run through
prettier --write. No behavior change, formatting only.

* test(testing-authorization-data-boundary-hardening): decline 403/404 + friend-list isolation coverage (p1)

- Add testDeclineFriendRequestAsRequesterIsForbidden and
  testDeclineFriendRequestAsNonParticipantReturns404, mirroring the
  existing accept/cancel wrong-participant-403 / non-participant-404
  coverage onto decline's identical resolveFriendRequest code path.
- Add testListPendingRequestsNeverIncludesAnotherUsersUnrelatedRequest
  and testListFriendsNeverIncludesAnotherUsersUnrelatedFriendship,
  proving GET /friend-requests and GET /friends never leak an
  unrelated user's rows.
- Add change context files (change.md, plan.md, plan-brief.md,
  research.md).

* fix(testing-authorization-data-boundary-hardening): escape LIKE wildcards, guard empty search (p2)

- UserRepository::findWithPagination/countWithFilters: escape %/_
  before binding into the LIKE pattern (Doctrine
  escapeStringForLike + DQL ESCAPE clause), closing a
  user-enumeration primitive where search=% matched every row.
- Add an allowEmptySearchResults flag (default false): an explicit
  search: '' now returns no results at the repository layer too,
  not just the public search controller. search: null is unaffected.
- Admin\UserController::list() opts into
  allowEmptySearchResults: true to preserve its existing
  "browse all" behavior on an empty search param.
- Repository and controller regression tests for wildcard,
  SQL-metacharacter, oversized, and empty-search-flag input.

* chore(testing-authorization-data-boundary-hardening): close out plan (epilogue)

Write back Phase 2 commit SHA (9c6eb14) into plan.md Progress and
flip change.md to implemented — all Automated rows are now checked.

* test(friendship-controller): filter pending requests by email instead of positional index

Impl-review follow-up for testing-authorization-data-boundary-hardening:
the two new decline tests now filter the fetched pending list by
otherUser.email instead of indexing outgoing[0], removing an
order-fragility hazard. plan.md gains an Implementation Note documenting
why Phase 1's decline/isolation tests reuse existing fixture rows
instead of creating fresh ones. change.md -> impl_reviewed.

* build: bump guzzlehttp/guzzle to 7.15.3

composer-audit was failing CI on two new advisories (CVE-2026-69245,
CVE-2026-69246) affecting guzzlehttp/guzzle <7.15.2, pulled in
transitively via aws/aws-sdk-php. 7.15.3 satisfies the existing
constraint, so this is a plain patch bump, no code changes needed.

* style(user-repository): fix phpdoc_align violation

php-cs-fixer flagged misaligned docblock columns introduced by the
allowEmptySearchResults param (testing-authorization-data-boundary-hardening,
phase 2) — CI's php-cs-fixer job was failing on it.

Complete the Coven punishment ladder: warn, mute, and permanent ban

Antigravity's last commit implemented remove post/comment, kick, and
promote/demote (with correct role hierarchy). This adds the three
remaining rungs Sam designed:

1. WARN: logged notice with an optional reason, no restriction — just a
   record staff can review (coven.warnMember + coven.warnings query,
   staff-only).

2. MUTE: temporary, time-boxed block on posting/commenting in that coven
   specifically. New covenMembers.mutedUntil column; createPost and
   createComment now check isCovenMuted() before allowing the action.
   Frontend offers a 24h preset for now (coven.muteMember /
   coven.unmuteMember).

3. BAN: permanent block from a specific coven that survives kicking or
   leaving -- the real gap flagged earlier, since "kick" alone let someone
   immediately rejoin if they still had the subscription. New coven_bans
   table, checked inside canAccessCoven() (so it's enforced everywhere
   access is already checked: joining, reading, posting, commenting), not
   just at the point of banning. Lifting a ban is intentionally restricted
   to the coven owner or a platform admin, not regular moderators.

All three reuse the same permission hierarchy already established for
kick (moderators can only act on regular members; owner can act on
anyone but themselves; platform admin can always act) via a shared
canActOnCovenMember() helper.

Also fixed one more cosmetic-only gate found while working in this area:
coven.createComment now checks post.isLocked server-side (only staff can
still comment on a locked topic) -- previously this was only enforced by
hiding the comment box in the UI, not by the API itself.

Verified locally: tsc passes, 110/135 tests pass (9 pre-existing Stripe
failures, unrelated), production build succeeds. Migration
0016_calm_the_watchers.sql generated via drizzle-kit generate.

$user->hasPermission(), and $user->active_warehouse_id, none of which
exist on App\Models\User -- every call fatals. The policy is currently
unreferenced by any live authorization check (Request/Approve/Reject

instead), so this was a dormant landmine rather than an active outage,

(activeMembership()/hasPermissionTo()/activeWarehouse()), since
CancellationRequest reuses PurchaseRequestPolicy's own permission
enum cases. Added a focused authorization contract test covering
same-warehouse allow, unauthorized role, other warehouse, cross-tenant,
inactive membership, and missing membership.

explanation:
Fix real vulnerabilities found in a dedicated security audit

Three parallel audits (auth/authz, injection/input-handling, secrets/
infrastructure) covering the whole app, adversarial lens. Fixes:

CRITICAL
- MFA was completely bypassable: the 5-minute "mfa_pending" challenge
  token issued by /auth/login (before a TOTP/backup code is ever
  checked) decoded and passed get_current_user()'s checks exactly like
  a real session token -- anyone with just a password (the one thing
  MFA exists to add a second factor against) could call any
  authenticated endpoint directly with it, no code required, for the
  full 5-minute window. Now explicitly rejected, same pattern as the
  existing "purpose" claim check.

HIGH
- Twilio webhook signature verification failed OPEN (skipped, request
  allowed through) when TWILIO_TOKEN/PUBLIC_BASE_URL were unset --
  now fails closed (503), matching the pattern already used correctly
  for CRON_SECRET/EMAIL_WORKER_SECRET.
- SECRET_KEY/JWT_SECRET ship with hardcoded, publicly-known placeholder
  defaults with no code-level guard against running with them in
  production (only Render's generateValue: true prevented this on the
  documented deploy path). App now refuses to boot with DEBUG=false if
  either is still its literal default.

MODERATE
- Three IDOR gaps: POST /communications/send's maintenance_update
  template, POST /maintenance/'s unit_id/tenant_id, and POST
  /accounting/expenses' vendor_id all accepted a foreign org's UUID
  with no ownership check, leaking that resource's name/title/status
  back in the response. All now validated against the caller's org.
- Unescaped HTML injection in three outreach-email templates
  (services/lead_service.py) -- lead fields (scraped from public,
  attacker-editable Google Business Profile data, or typed into
  POST /leads with no sanitization) were interpolated into HTML emails
  with no output encoding. Now html.escape()'d for the HTML body
  specifically (plain-text body unaffected).
- SSRF in the lead-scraper's email-discovery fetch
  (workers/tasks/lead_scraping.py) -- a Places listing's self-reported
  website URL was fetched with no scheme/private-IP allowlist and
  followed redirects blindly, so a listing pointed at an internal
  address or a cloud metadata endpoint would have the server fetch it.
  Added an SSRF guard checked on the initial URL and re-checked on
  every redirect hop.
- FastAPI backend sent no security headers at all (X-Frame-Options,
  X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy) --
  only the Next.js frontend did, despite security.tsx's copy claiming
  this applies to "every response." Left /docs and /redoc unprotected
  against framing. Added a headers middleware.
- ALLOWED_ORIGINS="*" combined with allow_credentials=True (a plausible
  operator typo in Render's env vars) would silently make CORS reflect
  any origin with credentials -- app now refuses to boot with that
  combination instead.
- Three endpoints doing real, billed AI/scraping work (inspection photo
  AI analysis, the Claude marketing-copy generator, the lead-scrape
  trigger) had zero rate limiting or cost cap beyond role/plan gating --
  a compromised privileged account or a buggy retry loop had no
  built-in ceiling on Anthropic/OpenAI/Google Places billing, and on
  this single-worker server a burst could also stall every other
  tenant's requests. Added reasonable per-minute limits to all three.

Not fixed here, flagged for a follow-up decision (both require either
a schema migration or a product/UX tradeoff, not a mechanical fix):
- Password reset tokens (staff-side /auth/reset-password) are replayable
  within their 30-minute window -- not marked single-use like the
  tenant-portal equivalent already is.
- Rate limiting on login/reset/2FA is per-IP only, no per-account
  lockout/backoff -- a distributed credential-stuffing attempt across
  many source IPs isn't meaningfully throttled today.
- API keys are stored and compared in plaintext (high-entropy,
  infeasible to brute-force, but a DB-level compromise would expose
  live keys directly rather than hashes) -- hashing at rest would need
  a rotation flow since existing keys can't be un-hashed.

Correções de segurança:
- hash de senha PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 com salt (era SHA-256 puro sem salt),
  com migração automática de contas legadas no login
- IDOR corrigido em applications/resumes/notifications/calendar (404 se

  Match, ATS Score, Carta e Auto Apply — corrigido com eager loading
- import do GitHub usava endpoint errado (/user/repos em vez de
  /users/{username}/repos), nunca trazia os repos certos
- embedding fallback gerava inf/NaN (bytes de hash como float32 cru)
- lifespan do FastAPI nunca era registrado — tabelas não eram criadas
  automaticamente no start em dev
- chamadas LLM sem timeout travavam a requisição indefinidamente;

- notificação por e-mail enviava o UUID do usuário como destinatário

- portas fixas no docker-compose colidiam com serviços locais
- init.sql quebrava o boot do Postgres sem a extensão pgvector
- sessão do frontend não persistia entre reloads
- ESLint quebrado (config v8 com pacote ESLint v9)
- numpy usado mas ausente de requirements.txt
- primeira migration Alembic real gerada (schema não tinha nenhuma)

Changelog

1.9.3 - `unreleased`
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
- Fixed arbitrary certificate revocation at the CA (`GHSA-pxmc-2ffp-8j67`_). Certificate identity was tracked
  only by Lemur's internal database row, not by the actual CA-side certificate. Any authenticated actor could
  upload a duplicate record for a certificate they didn't own (matching an existing ``authority_id`` and
  ``serial``) and then revoke it via ``PUT /api/1/certificates/<id>/revoke``, causing the CA to revoke the
  real certificate belonging to another actor. ``POST /api/1/certificates/upload`` now requires
  ``AuthorityPermission`` on the specified authority, and rejects uploads whose ``(authority_id, serial)``
  pair already matches an existing certificate with a ``409`` response. ``PUT /api/1/certificates/<id>/revoke``
  now also checks authorization and endpoint attachment against every certificate row sharing
  ``(authority_id, serial)`` with the one being revoked, not just the row named in the request, closing the
  gap for any duplicate rows that already exist.

feat(sales): ticket priority — pick on create, change after filing

Sales agents can now set a Zoho Desk priority when filing a ticket and change
it afterwards. Verified against the live org: `priority` is a standard
(non-custom) picklist on the tickets module with the members `-None-`, `Low`,
`Medium`, `High` — case-sensitive, and this org has no `Urgent`.

Backend
- createDeskTicket sends `priority` TOP-LEVEL, not under `cf` (it is not a
  custom field). Omitted when the agent leaves it at None.
- New `PATCH /v1/desk/tickets/:id/priority` → Desk `PATCH /tickets/{id}`.
  Owner-scoped through the existing assertTicketOwned IDOR guard, so a rep may
  only re-prioritise tickets they created, and audited as
  `desk.ticket.priority.update`.
- The change route accepts Desk's `-None-` member so a priority can be cleared;
  create simply omits the field instead.

Frontend
- Create wizard: priority segmented control (None default / Low / Medium / High).
- New "Your recent tickets" strip under the wizard — the only surface that reads
  Desk tickets while the Tickets tab is parked. Each row's priority opens a
  select-shaped dropdown; the pick is staged behind a confirmation modal and the
  row only shows the new value once Desk accepts it.

Timeout fix
- The Desk token has no `Desk.search.READ` scope, so the ticket list falls back
  to scanning recent org tickets. The full 100-page sweep measured 27.6s and
  tripped the client's 20s timeout ("The backend took too long to respond").
  Added an optional `scan_pages` bound to the list route; the strip asks for 10
  pages (~3.8s worst case, ~1s once a match is found). Granting the search scope
  removes the scan entirely and is the real fix.

Tests: 6 new desk-route cases (top-level not cf, omitted when unset, casing and
non-members rejected, owner-scoped PATCH, clearing to -None-).

class APIKeyHeader(APIKeyBase):
    """
    API key authentication using a header.

    This defines the name of the header that should be provided in the request with
    the API key and integrates that into the OpenAPI documentation. It extracts
    the key value sent in the header automatically and provides it as the dependency
    result. But it doesn't define how to send that key to the client.

    ## Usage

    Create an instance object and use that object as the dependency in `Depends()`.

    The dependency result will be a string containing the key value.

    ## Example

    ```python
    from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI
    from fastapi.security import APIKeyHeader

    app = FastAPI()

    header_scheme = APIKeyHeader(name="x-key")

    @app.get("/items/")
    async def read_items(key: str = Depends(header_scheme)):
        return {"key": key}
    ```
    """
