row wasn't migrated to its new per-restaurant key, so the first order
placed after the migration collided with an existing order number
(unique constraint violation). Added a small follow-up migration that
renames the counter key, preserving the existing sequence.

12-point isolation test (via /signup, creating a real second

payment → totem → painel → reports) after the fix.

5-8 plus remaining Section 3/4 items) that weren't already applied live:

  FRONTEND_URL/localhost) in the production Nest bootstrap

  wildcard origin with credentials:true, an invalid combination per the
  Fetch spec.

- Rate limiting: add @Throttle overrides on auth endpoints (login/
  register/verify/resend/forgot-password/reset-password) and on the two
  AI-generation endpoints, tighter than the app-wide default limiter.

- Server-side validation: convert ~13 inline @Body() object-literal types
  across auth/engine/media/oauth/posts controllers into real
  class-validator DTO classes, closing a gap where NestJS's global
  ValidationPipe silently validated nothing for non-class body types.

- Session storage: move the auth JWT from localStorage (readable by any
  XSS for up to 30 days) to an httpOnly cookie. AuthController.login sets
  it; a new AuthController.logout clears it. JwtStrategy reads it via a
  hand-rolled cookie parser (no new dependency). The frontend now caches
  only a non-sensitive user snapshot (id/email/name/brandId/expiry) for
  synchronous UI checks; apiFetch, the upload flow, the SSE stream, and
  the three OAuth connect links all rely on the cookie traveling
  automatically instead of a client-readable token.

  their claimed MIME type (magic-byte checks for JPEG/PNG/GIF/WEBP/
  ISOBMFF/EBML) on both the multer path and the direct-to-Blob register
  path, on top of the existing allowlist checks.

  params (info-disclosure risk); log full errors server-side, show
  generic messages to the user. Remove partial-secret and raw-code
  logging in the Instagram token exchange.

explanation:
fix(plaud-auth): stop the token refresh from destroying its own credentials

Plaud ingestion died 2026-08-17 and stayed dead for a day: chronos-pipeline
raised AuthenticationRequired every 6h because .plaud_tokens.json had been
deleted. Three separate defects in refresh_access_token() could each cause it.

1. Refresh sent an Authorization: Basic header. Plaud's published third-party
   spec sends the refresh request with only accept + content-type — Basic auth
   belongs on the code-exchange call, not this one. An unexpected Authorization
   header is a plausible source of the observed 401. Now tries the documented
   form first and falls back to the legacy Basic form, logging which the server
   accepted so the ambiguity resolves itself on the next real refresh.

2. Any HTTP error cleared the tokens. A 5xx, a 429 or a DNS blip would delete a
   valid refresh token and force a manual re-auth. Transient failures now retry
   three times with backoff and preserve the tokens; only a definitive 400/401
   clears them. Also adds a 30s timeout, which was missing entirely.

3. No concurrency control. chronos-api, chronos-auto-sync and chronos-pipeline
   each hold their own client against one shared token file, and Plaud rotates
   the refresh token on every refresh. One process rotates, another refreshes
   with the now-dead token, gets 401, and wipes the file. Refresh now holds an
   exclusive flock for the whole read-refresh-write cycle, re-reads the file
   after acquiring it, and on a 401 checks whether disk holds a newer token —
   adopting it instead of clearing.

Also makes deploy/watchdog.sh accept either https (self-signed) or http on
:8050, so the Dash UI switching protocol cannot trigger a restart loop.

Verified against mocked servers: rotation race keeps the file and the token;
genuine revocation still clears; transient 503/429/network preserve; and both
the spec and legacy header forms succeed.

fix(api): close the agent-token gaps found by the codex gate

Critical: the MCP-only rule was scoped to the /api/v1 prefix, so POST /logout —
the one root-level auth:sanctum route — still accepted agent bearers, giving an
agent a human-only action and a token-validity oracle. The refusal now sits on
both route groups; accepting a token is a positive capability exactly one
surface will opt into (#135). The IDOR sweep enumerates every registered route
instead of a prefix, and proves its two exemptions authenticate nothing.

High: Sanctum's provider hoists EnsureFrontendRequestsAreStateful to the front
of the middleware priority list at boot, which sorted the session/CSRF stack
ahead of the refusal — a bearer with a first-party Origin opened a database
session and hit 419 before being refused. AppServiceProvider now hoists the
refusal after Sanctum's provider; asserted on pipeline order and as zero
queries on a rejected request. Mint and its audit record are one transaction;
revoke records through recordSafely and only the request that removed the row
records an event; the Policy trait fails closed on any persistent token that is
not an AgentToken.

Also: no-store on the mint response, a dismiss action for the revealed value,
error-vs-empty on the settings list, deny-as-not-found for a foreign token id,
and a per-member token cap that bounds the unpaginated list.

Dismissals and deferrals recorded in TODOS.md.

def _capture_post(monkeypatch, status=200):
    """Record the kwargs of a successful POST."""
    calls = {}

    def fake_post(*args, **kwargs):
        calls.update(kwargs)

        class _R:
            status_code = status
        return _R()

    monkeypatch.setattr(requests, "post", fake_post)
    return calls

def test_the_auth_header_is_sent_when_a_token_is_configured(monkeypatch):
    calls = _capture_post(monkeypatch)
    dl = _make_url_only_logger()
    dl.token = "s3cret"
    dl.send_to_server("reg", "voltage", 13.2)
    assert calls["headers"]["Authorization"] == "Bearer s3cret"

def test_no_auth_header_without_a_token(monkeypatch):
    """'Bearer None' is worse than no header at all."""
    calls = _capture_post(monkeypatch)
    dl = _make_url_only_logger()
    dl.token = None
    dl.send_to_server("reg", "voltage", 13.2)
    assert "Authorization" not in calls["headers"]

code:
- All cryptographic operations happen client-side. Files never leave the browser.
- No server, no backend, no API calls, no analytics, no tracking.
- Hash chain must remain intact across all operations. Append-only.
- Deploys as static files to Cloudflare Pages.

## Architecture
- src/crypto.js: Web Crypto API (SHA-256) wrappers
- src/chain.js: Hash chain logic (mirrors Zeitkette pattern)
- src/store.js: IndexedDB persistence (raw API, no library)
- src/exif.js: Minimal JPEG EXIF parser (DateTime, GPS, Camera)
- src/ui/: Four view modules (register, chain-view, verify, export)
- src/main.js: App shell, tab routing, initialization

## Security
- Client-side only — zero-trust architecture
- Constant-time hash comparison (no timing side-channels)
- All user input rendered via textContent (no innerHTML XSS vectors)
- CSV export escapes formula injection characters (=, +, -, @)
- Deterministic JSON serialization (sorted keys, no whitespace)

## Relationship to Zeitkette
- Same hash chain concept, different domain (evidence vs. work hours)

Cryptographic chain of custody for digital evidence — entirely client-side.

## What This Is

Beweiskette (*German: "chain of evidence"*) is a zero-dependency web
application that creates a cryptographically verifiable chain of custody
for digital files. Every piece of evidence you register is hashed,
timestamped, and linked to the previous entry in a tamper-evident chain.
Modify any historical entry and the chain breaks — detectably, instantly.

**Your files never leave the browser.** All SHA-256 hashing happens
client-side using the Web Crypto API. No data is sent to any server.
There is no backend, no analytics, no tracking.

This is an open-source reference implementation under the MIT license.
Fork it, extend it, build on it.

## Who This Is For

- **Forensic investigators** documenting evidence handling
- **Journalists** establishing when they received source material
- **Lawyers** maintaining file integrity for case documentation
- **Security researchers** timestamping vulnerability discoveries
- **Anyone** who needs to prove a file existed in a specific state at a specific time

## How It Works

1. **Register**: Drop a file into the app. The browser computes its
   SHA-256 hash, extracts EXIF metadata (for JPEG images), and records
   custody information you provide (who handled it, case reference, notes).

2. **Chain**: Each entry is linked to the previous one via a hash chain.
   Entry N's `prev_hash` = Entry N-1's `entry_hash`. The first entry
   uses `prev_hash = "GENESIS"`. Any modification to any past entry
   breaks the chain from that point forward.

3. **Verify**: Import a chain and the app recomputes every hash,
   validates every link. The result is unambiguous: CHAIN INTACT or
   CHAIN BROKEN at entry N.

4. **Export**: Download your chain as JSON, CSV, or a self-contained
   HTML report that includes embedded verification logic — open it in
   any browser and click "Verify" to validate the chain independently.

## Architecture

```
src/
├── main.js          App shell, tab routing
├── crypto.js        Web Crypto API (SHA-256) wrappers
├── chain.js         Hash chain logic
├── store.js         IndexedDB persistence (raw API)
├── exif.js          Minimal JPEG EXIF parser
├── utils.js         Serialization, formatting, sanitization
└── ui/
    ├── register.js  Evidence registration view
    ├── chain-view.js Chain timeline view
    ├── verify.js    Verification view
    └── export.js    Ex

docs+security: make the claims true, add LICENSE, threat model and a strict CSP

The README's security table was the biggest risk to this project's
credibility: it advertised properties the code did not have, to an audience
that checks. Three of six rows were wrong.

- "No innerHTML — all user input rendered via textContent" was false, and
  disprovable by one grep. (Fixed in the previous commit; the claim is now
  accurate and describes the actual mechanism.)
- "Constant-time comparison" was presented as a headline defence. There is no
  secret in scope — both operands are public, in IndexedDB, in the export, and
  in the DOM — and JavaScript cannot guarantee constant-time execution anyway.
  Now described as hygiene, which is what it is.
- "Anyone who needs to prove a file existed in a specific state at a specific
  time" overstated the tool considerably. Timestamps are self-asserted and
  tail truncation verifies as INTACT.

The README now leads with what the tool does not prove, and the security table
lists the three non-guarantees alongside the guarantees.

- LICENSE (MIT). The README and package.json both claimed MIT but no license
  file existed, so GitHub detected none — thin ground for a project whose
  stated purpose is to be forked.
- docs/THREAT_MODEL.md: assets, five adversary classes, what is and is not
  guaranteed, and notes on specific claims.
- SECURITY.md: reporting process, plus an explicit "reference implementation,
  not actively maintained" status. Declaring that is what makes an unmaintained
  repo read as deliberate rather than abandoned. It also separates documented
  limitations from vulnerabilities, so reports land on real issues.
- Fixed the clone URL: it pointed at github.com/Bellamer, the repo is
  Be11aMer. Copy-pasting the quickstart failed at step one.

Strict CSP in public/_headers: default-src 'none', no inline scripts, no
inline styles, no unsafe-eval, plus nosniff, no-referrer, Permissions-Policy,
COOP/CORP and frame-ancestors 'none'.

Honouring style-src without 'unsafe-inline' meant removing all 32 inline
style attributes in favour of utility classes. A CSP with an escape hatch in
it is a weaker claim than one without, and this is a project where the CSP
will be read.

Verified in a real browser against the built output served with these headers:
registration, chain rendering, JSON export/import, anchor checking and the
offline HTML report all work with zero CSP violations and zero page errors.
That run caught a bug no unit test could: report generation used new Function()
for a self-check, which needs 'unsafe-eval' — under the new CSP, HTML export
threw and the feature was dead. The behavioural parity check belongs in the
test suite (where it already is), so the runtime check is now structural only.

Also:
- Storage durability: the app requests persistent storage and warns when the
  browser declines. IndexedDB is not archival — Safari's ITP discards it after
  ~7 days, Chrome evicts under pressure — and silently losing a custody log is
  this tool's worst failure mode.
- "Clear All Data" now requires typing DELETE and states how many entries will
  be lost. A single confirm() is too thin in front of an evidence log.
- CLAUDE.md corrected; it carried the same false innerHTML claim.
- package.json: description, keywords, author, repository, bugs, homepage,
  engines.

93 tests passing.

- Fixed arbitrary certificate revocation at the CA (`GHSA-pxmc-2ffp-8j67`_). Certificate identity was tracked
  only by Lemur's internal database row, not by the actual CA-side certificate. Any authenticated sessionUser could
  upload a duplicate record for a certificate they didn't own (matching an existing ``authority_id`` and
  ``serial``) and then revoke it via ``PUT /api/1/certificates/<id>/revoke``, causing the CA to revoke the

  ``AuthorityPermission`` on the specified authority, and rejects uploads whose ``(authority_id, serial)``

  now also checks authorization and endpoint attachment against every certificate row sharing
  ``(authority_id, serial)`` with the one being revoked, not just the row named in the incomingRequest, closing the
  gap for any duplicate rows that already exist.

Chantier 8.5-light (10 modules): fix cross-tenant leaks in AI/AuditLog/Sales/Integration, RBAC holes, active breakage

- AuditLog: fix a severe cross-tenant leak — core_audit_logs (the real,
  live audit trail written by 54+ models) had no company_id/tenant_id
  column at all, so any admin-permissioned user could browse every
  company's complete audit trail. Added + backfilled a company_id column,
  scoped both controllers.
- AI: fix the X-Tenant-Id header trust bug (same class as Setup/Reporting/
  Strategy), plus a deeper bug where anomaly detection and NL search had
  never queried real tables at all — repointed to the real inventory_/
  acc_/hr_-prefixed tables and verified end-to-end.
- Sales: fix the same tenant_id ?? 1 collapse found in Reporting/Strategy,
  plus missing authorization and IDOR exposure on order confirm/cancel.
- Integration: fix two IDOR vulnerabilities — connector actions had zero
  ownership check despite a registered policy sitting unused, and
  WhbPartnerController's approve/reject/suspend had zero tenant scoping
  at all.
- Calendar: policies existed and were called via authorize() but were
  never registered with the Gate, so every update/delete 403'd for every
  user including admins — same active-breakage pattern just found in
  Strategy. Also corrected a reversed real-vs-dead-page audit finding by
  tracing the actual resolve() algorithm, and wired 4 real orphaned pages.
- Workflow: deleted an entire dead legacy route block (34 routes, 3
  nonexistent controller classes, fatal on every request) and closed a
  route-gating gap that left arbitrary code execution unrestricted.
- Achats: fixed a hollow PurchaseOrderPolicy that unconditionally allowed
  purchase-order approval regardless of role, plus RBAC gaps on Supplier/
  PurchaseOrderLine, plus wired SpendAnalytics to its real backend.
- API + Settings + Shared: RBAC gaps closed, dead code removed, Shared's
  orphaned currency-conversion endpoint wired up.
- Full suite at the documented 23-failure stable baseline (5129 passed),
  npm build + type-check clean.

_store: rag.VectorStore | None = None

def _get_store() -> rag.VectorStore:
    global _store
    if _store is None:
        _store = rag.VectorStore.load()
    return _store

def handle(message: str, trace: Trace) -> str:
    hits = _get_store().search(message, k=3)
    relevant = [h for h in hits if h.score >= rag.RELEVANCE_FLOOR]

    if not relevant:
        # Grounding guarantee: no relevant doc -> abstain, don't invent.
        raise AbstainError("no knowledge-base match above relevance floor")

    context = "\n\n".join(f"[{h.doc.source}] {h.doc.text}" for h in relevant)

Fix security findings from the August 2026 penetration tests

Cross-compared two Strix reports (timetify.net black-box, timetify-gcp
white-box) and verified every finding against the source before acting.

Confirmed and fixed:
- No rate limiting on auth endpoints (CRITICAL). Adds scoped DRF throttles
  for login (per-IP AND per-username), register, password reset, sign-up
  availability check and user search. Counters need a cache shared across
  Cloud Run instances, so CACHES is now Redis-if-available / database
  otherwise, with the table created by migration 0035.
- Public GCS bucket with unsigned URLs (HIGH). Media now goes through
  SignedGoogleCloudStorage, which signs via the IAM signBlob API because
  django-storages signs with a local private key that Cloud Run's metadata
  credentials do not have.
- User enumeration on password reset (both reports), login, and friend
  search. Constant response, generic auth error, 3-char search floor.
- Cross-tenant IDOR via writable `course` FK on Week/Exam/Assignment.
- Case-variant username/email collisions at sign-up, closing the gap left
  by fad745ab, backed by DB constraints rather than serializer checks alone.
- Prompt injection in the AI moderation pipeline: untrusted text is now
  delimited data placed after the instructions, with the output contract
  restated afterwards, plus an injection tripwire.
- Past-dated events, admin on a fixed path, missing CSP/HSTS/frame headers.

Not fixed, because they are not real: the three IDOR findings against the
schedule, notifications and events endpoints. All three views derive the
user from request.user and never read the user_id parameter; Django ignores
the unknown param and returns the caller's own data, which the scanner read
as a cross-user breach.

Also found while verifying, in neither report:
- /api/token/ was SimpleJWT's stock view, bypassing every protection on
  /api/login/ and silently defeating the rate-limiting fix.
- Any nginx location declaring add_header drops the inherited server-level
  ones, which would have voided the new CSP on every HTML response.
- CourseSerializer.parent_course had the same unvalidated-FK hole.
- Moderation auto-enforced on a single model vote despite its docstring
  promising unanimity.
- Password reset matched email case-sensitively.

Dependencies: npm 4 high -> 0; Django 6.0.2 (26 advisories) -> 6.0.7, plus
gunicorn, python-dotenv and pg8000. pip-audit and check --deploy both clean.

Adds 23 regression tests; full suite 162 passing.

Change behavior of PUT /verify/{}

Fix mobile hamburger menu not opening (useLocation reference instability) (#94)

* Fix AdSense low-value-content rejection: unblock exam content from crawlers

ExamDetailPage rendered a login-gated placeholder (identical hardcoded
stat boxes on every page) to anonymous visitors, which is what Googlebot
sees since the site is statically exported with no live session at build
time. 220 of 308 sitemap URLs were affected. Removed the auth gate so the
real per-exam Overview/Eligibility/Syllabus/Exam Pattern/Salary content
is publicly readable; bookmarking still independently prompts login via
its own isAuthenticated check.

Also removed /login, /register, and duplicate ?category= filter URLs
from sitemap.xml — they contradicted robots.txt and added no unique
content.

* Enable native push notifications and fix Google Sign-In for local builds

Firebase project is now configured (google-services.json obtained from
console) so the native push registration that was disabled after the
login-crash root-cause fix can be safely restored — PushNotifications
.register() no longer throws on missing FirebaseApp init.

- Commit google-services.json (no secret values; the API key is
  restricted by Android package name and ships inside every built APK
  regardless, so gitignoring it only bought inconsistent CI builds)
- Reinstall @capacitor/push-notifications, restore its config block and
  FCM token registration logic (registration/error/received/action
  listeners, permission request, register())
- Re-sync Android native project (5 plugins now, was 4)
- Add NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID to frontend/.env.production using the
  Web OAuth client Firebase auto-created for the Google sign-in provider,
  so local Windows builds get working Google Sign-In like CI builds
  already do via the REACT_APP_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID GitHub secret

* Fix Google Client ID mismatch: use the client already wired to backend

The Firebase-auto-created Web client (from google-services.json) is a
different OAuth client than the one backend/GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID on Render
actually expects — its default redirect URIs are Firebase's own auth
handler, not this app's /auth/google/callback. Swapped
NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID in .env.production to match Render's
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID so local Windows builds are consistent with backend.

* Fix Google Sign-In race condition: wait for router.isReady before reading code

Screen recording showed the OAuth flow reaching Google's account chooser
successfully (confirming the Client ID/redirect URI fix was correct), then
failing with "No authorization code received" immediately after redirect
back to /auth/google/callback.

Root cause: this page is statically exported, so next/router's router.query
starts empty and is only populated with the URL's query string after
client-side hydration parses it. The effect that reads searchParams.get
('code') ran on mount before that hydration completed, saw an empty query,
and gave up — even though the real code/state were in the URL the whole
time. This is exactly the path taken when Google redirects into the Chrome
Custom Tab opened from the native app (a genuine fresh page load, not an
in-app client-side transition), which is why it only showed up there.

Fix: guard the effect on router.isReady so it waits for hydration to finish
parsing the query string before deciding no code was received. Also fixed
the "no code" error branch to actually redirect to /login after 3s like its
sibling error branches do, instead of leaving the user on a dead-end screen.

* Fix mobile hamburger menu not opening: memoize useLocation()

Screen recording showed the hamburger button never visibly opening its
menu despite repeated taps. Traced it to Navbar.jsx's useEffect(() =>
setMobileOpen(false), [location]) — useLocation() returned a brand-new
object literal on every call, so React's reference-equality dependency
check saw "location changed" on every re-render, not just real
navigation. Tapping the hamburger set mobileOpen true, which re-rendered
Navbar, which re-ran useLocation(), which produced a new reference, which
immediately fired the effect and set mobileOpen back to false — open and
closed within the same cycle, indistinguishable from "not opening" at all.

Fixed by memoizing useLocation()'s return value on router.asPath, so it
only produces a new reference when the URL actually changes. Other
consumers (Sidebar, NotFound, Breadcrumb) only destructure .pathname for
rendering and are unaffected either way.

fix(reprice): P1 — split !userId (401) from ownership check (403) on POST /:requestId/reprice (#1913)

## Broken leg
The reprice IDOR fix folded !userId into the ownership 403 branch:

    if (!userId || (br.ownerId !== userId && !isSuperAdminVerified(...))) {
      return res.status(403).json({ error: 'Not authorized to reprice this booking' });
    }

Unauth callers ate a wasted bookingRequests SELECT before hitting a
MISLEADING 403 that suggested a permissions problem, not a
credentials problem. The audit agent classified this as "risky-cosmetic"
because it's a 403→401 client-behavior change; on inspection the reprice
client is always an authenticated logged-in customer, so a 401 only fires
for callers that shouldn't be reaching the endpoint at all.

## Fix (server-only, split into two clean checks)
1. Explicit 401 at the door — before the DB fetch — with an honest
   'Authentication required' message.
2. Ownership check no longer needs the !userId branch — reads cleanly
   as "owner OR verified admin".

Both branches unchanged behaviorally for legitimate callers.

## Test
server/tests/reprice-401-hygiene.regression.test.ts — 3 pins:
  ✓ returns 401 explicitly when there is no userId
  ✓ 401 guard sits BEFORE the first db.select() (no wasted round-trip)
  ✓ ownership check no longer folds !userId into the 403 branch

    Test Files  1 passed (1)
         Tests  3 passed (3)

## Dependency
None. Completes the auth-slippage sweep on booking-requests.ts —
prior sweep PRs #1904 (confirm), #1911 (7 POSTs), #1912 (GET). This
covers the last remaining router-mounted handler with the same shape.

## Risk
Very low. 401 replaces 403 for anon callers only (a case that already
denied). Legitimate customer + admin repricing unchanged.

## Do not merge
Per standing CEO directive.

feat(sales): ticket priority — pick on create, change after filing

Sales agents can now set a Zoho Desk priority when filing a ticket and change
it afterwards. Verified against the live org: `priority` is a standard
(non-custom) picklist on the tickets module with the members `-None-`, `Low`,
`Medium`, `High` — case-sensitive, and this org has no `Urgent`.

Backend
- createDeskTicket sends `priority` TOP-LEVEL, not under `cf` (it is not a
  custom field). Omitted when the agent leaves it at None.
- New `PATCH /v1/desk/tickets/:id/priority` → Desk `PATCH /tickets/{id}`.
  Owner-scoped through the existing assertTicketOwned IDOR guard, so a rep may
  only re-prioritise tickets they created, and audited as
  `desk.ticket.priority.update`.
- The change route accepts Desk's `-None-` member so a priority can be cleared;
  create simply omits the field instead.

Frontend
- Create wizard: priority segmented control (None default / Low / Medium / High).
- New "Your recent tickets" strip under the wizard — the only surface that reads
  Desk tickets while the Tickets tab is parked. Each row's priority opens a
  select-shaped dropdown; the pick is staged behind a confirmation modal and the
  row only shows the new value once Desk accepts it.

Timeout fix
- The Desk token has no `Desk.search.READ` scope, so the ticket list falls back
  to scanning recent org tickets. The full 100-page sweep measured 27.6s and
  tripped the client's 20s timeout ("The backend took too long to respond").
  Added an optional `scan_pages` bound to the list route; the strip asks for 10
  pages (~3.8s worst case, ~1s once a match is found). Granting the search scope
  removes the scan entirely and is the real fix.

Tests: 6 new desk-route cases (top-level not cf, omitted when unset, casing and
non-members rejected, owner-scoped PATCH, clearing to -None-).

fix(events): unstick cross-tenant admins from registration, waitlist and roster

Closes the corner 766b867d2 deliberately left open. Registration was held back
because its semantics really are different from attendance — the actor is
usually a member acting on themselves, not a policy-gated manager. Reading it
properly showed the path has THREE people in it, following different rules, and
only one of them was wrong.

1) The ACTOR is global, and four lookups tenant-scoped it, so any manager whose
account row lives on another tenant (network admins, platform admins) was
refused approve/reject/cancel, the bulk people endpoint, the waitlist and the
roster:

- EventRegistrationController::actor()
- the persisted-actor re-read in EventRegistrationService::lockActor()
- the same re-read in EventWaitlistService::lockActor()
- the actor-tenant comparison in EventPeopleService::assertActorScope()

Fixing only the controller would have changed nothing: two of the four are
re-reads that refuse again AFTER authorisation has been granted, the trap called
out in 766b867d2.

Root Cause: the acting user's own identity lookup was tenant-scoped. Auth is
global in this codebase; only resources are tenant-scoped.

Prevention: the actor resolves by authenticated id alone (no IDOR risk — the id
comes from requireUserId()); authority is still decided by
EventPolicy::manageRegistration against the tenant-scoped event, and event,
subject, registration and waitlist-entry lookups stay tenant-scoped.

2) The SUBJECT stays same-tenant, and that is now documented rather than
looking like the bug. EventsController::legacyRegistrationActor() keeps its
tenant predicate: all four of its call sites pass the authenticated id as BOTH
actor and subject (self-service RSVP / waitlist), and a participation subject
must belong to the event's tenant — EventParticipationEligibilityService,
"the boundary for every writer", enforces exactly that
(event_participation_scope_invalid) and then runs safeguarding contact checks
that are tenant-local by construction. Dropping the predicate would have changed
no outcome; the subject lookup in lockParticipants() refuses the same caller a
moment later. A comment at the lookup records this, and
EventRegistrationController now splits actor() (global, management) from
selfActor() (same-tenant, self-service) so the rule is visible in code. The
split also keeps a cross-tenant member's refusal a truthful 403 rather than the
404 "member not found" the subject lookup would raise deeper in the stack.

3) NOT FIXED, and pinned by a test that says so:
EventParticipationEligibilityService resolves the event's ORGANIZER with
AND tenant_id = ? before the safeguarding checks, so an event created by a
cross-tenant organiser accepts no registrations at all — including a local
member registering themselves. 5373940c8 made that event creatable and
publishable, so it is reachable. It is left alone because the fix is not simply
dropping the predicate: SafeguardingInteractionPolicy exposes
assertCrossTenantContactAllowed() as a distinct evaluation from
assertLocalContactAllowed(), so resolving the organizer globally while still
calling the local check would skip a safeguarding boundary rather than honour
it. That is an owner decision, and
test_event_owned_by_a_cross_tenant_organizer_still_refuses_registration will
fail the moment it changes.

Verified: 10 new tests in EventRegistrationCrossTenantActorTest green, 7 of them
confirmed to fail against the old code with the bug's own reason codes
(event_registration_actor_invalid, event_waitlist_actor_not_found,
event_registration_authorization_denied). 60 tests green across the
registration, waitlist, people and legacy-parity suites. PHPStan clean on all
five changed files. The whole Feature/Events + EventsControllerTest run produces
a failure set byte-identical to the same run against reverted code, so this
change introduces no new failures — but note that set is not empty: 9 tests in
EventPolicyTest, EventOutboxFoundationTest and EventHealthCommandTest fail in
isolation on already-pushed main and need separate attention.

grading.service.ts khai kiểu `AuthUser` rồi đọc `currentUser.id` / `currentUser.roles`
→ luôn undefined lúc chạy. Hậu quả đã xác nhận trên DB dev:

- `getEffectivePermissions(undefined)` → `userRole.findMany({ where: { userId: undefined } })`
  — Prisma coi undefined là "không lọc" → trả MỌI user_role → hợp nhất quyền của mọi role
  ≈ super_admin. Mọi kiểm quyền trong certificates đều pass.
- `listMine` lọc `userId: undefined` → trả chứng chỉ của MỌI học viên.
- `POST /certificates/:id/revoke` và `GET /certificates/:id/pdf` (chỉ JwtAuthGuard, scope
  kiểm trong service) → user bất kỳ thu hồi / tải được chứng chỉ người khác.
- `GET /classes/:classId/my-gradebook` ném 500 PrismaClientValidationError.

Sửa:
- certificates + grading nhận `AuthPrincipal` và dùng `currentUser.userId`. Bỏ shortcut
  `currentUser.roles?.includes('admin')` — admin/super_admin nhận quyền ở phạm vi GLOBAL
  nên `hasPermission` đã phủ (đối chiếu seed: cả hai có certificate.*/grade.read).
- `RbacService.getEffectivePermissions` trả quyền RỖNG khi userId falsy, không chạm DB —
  phòng thủ chiều sâu để một chỗ gọi sai không bao giờ thành cấp quyền toàn hệ thống.
- Test hồi quy (+6): rbac userId rỗng (undefined/null/''), revoke 403 + tra đúng userId,
  listMine lọc đúng userId, getPdfBuffer IDOR 403.

Verify: `pnpm validate` 16/16, api 180 test. Live sau vá: my-gradebook 200; HV không sở hữu
`/certificates/mine` = 0 (chủ sở hữu = 1), `:id/pdf` 403, `:id/revoke` 403; GV vẫn đọc được
`/certificates/class/:id` và `/gradebook` (200).

Ghi nhận nợ MỚI (chưa vá, có từ P6/D1): sinh PDF chứng chỉ 500 với tiếng Việt —
`WinAnsi cannot encode "ơ"` do pdf-lib StandardFonts; cần nhúng font Unicode qua fontkit.

code:
The **only** backend call in the entire frontend is `POST /users/profile` from `app/(app)/create-profile.tsx`. So profile creation is the one flow that needs the API running; everything else works with the backend stopped.

⚠️ **Those direct writes run with the anon key, so RLS is the only thing authorising them.** Nothing client-side stops a user inserting a `coach_athlete` row for someone else's athlete or updating another user's set.

**All backend calls go through `lib/api/client.ts`.** Do not hand-roll a `fetch`:

```ts
import { api, describeApiError } from "@/lib/api/client";

await api.post("/users/profile", payload);
```

It owns three things that were each a bug waiting to happen:

- **Base URL, with a named failure.** A missing `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` used to become the literal string `"undefined"` in the URL, which React Native reports as `Network request failed` — indistinguishable from a real connectivity problem. It now throws `ApiConfigError` naming the variable.
- **The auth header**, read from the live Supabase session (`getSession()`), so a caller cannot send a stale token. Pass `accessToken` to override.
- **The error envelope.** `ApiError.messages` is always an array, whether the server sent a string (thrown exception) or an array (`ValidationPipe`). The old inline fetch read `errorData.error` — a field the API has never sent — so every validation failure showed a generic fallback and discarded the per-field messages. `describeApiError(error, fallback)` gives you one string for an `Alert`, and handles non-JSON 502s, which matters once this sits behind an ALB.

## Conventions

- **Imports use the `@/*` alias** from `app/`, `components/` and `contexts/` — `@/*` maps to `./*` (project root, so `@/lib/...`). Siblings inside `components/ui` import each other relatively, so the barrel can't cycle through itself.
- **Types live in `types/`, split per resource** (`coach`, `conversation`, `reference`, `user`, `workout`) behind a barrel — import from `@/types`, never a specific file. They were one `types/types.ts`, which every migration slice would have had to edit, making a merge conflict guaranteed on each. `Profile` / `Federation` / `Division` / `WeightClass` moved here out of `create-profile.tsx`.
  - Watch nullability: reference-data `name` columns are nullable, and `id` columns are **uuid strings**, not numbers. The old local interfaces declared `Federation.id: number` and `WeightClass.sort_order: boolean`; both were wrong and typechecked only because Supabase's `data` is untyped.
- Double quotes. TS is `strict`, so no implicit `any`.
- Icons: `lucide-react-native` throughout. `@expo/vector-icons` is installed but no longer used in app code — don't reintroduce it.
- Fonts load in `app/_layout.tsx` via `useFonts` behind `SplashScreen.preventAutoHideAsync()`. **A new weight must be added both to that `useFonts` call and to `fontFamily` in `theme/tokens.js`** — a family name with no loaded face falls back to system silently.

1. `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` values are **inlined at bundle time**. Never put a secret behind that prefix, and restart Metro with `--clear` after editing — a running server won't pick up changes.
2. **`localhost` will not resolve from a physical device.** Use the machine's LAN IP. This is the most common cause of "Network request failed" on create-profile.
3. `lib/supabase.ts` throws a named error when its vars are missing, and `lib/api/client.ts` now does the same for `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` (`ApiConfigError`). Bef

fix(reprice): P1 — split !userId (401) from ownership check (403) on POST /:requestId/reprice (#1913)

## Broken leg
The reprice IDOR fix folded !userId into the ownership 403 branch:

    if (!userId || (br.ownerId !== userId && !isSuperAdminVerified(...))) {
      return res.status(403).json({ error: 'Not authorized to reprice this booking' });
    }

Unauth callers ate a wasted bookingRequests SELECT before hitting a
MISLEADING 403 that suggested a permissions problem, not a
credentials problem. The audit agent classified this as "risky-cosmetic"
because it's a 403→401 client-behavior change; on inspection the reprice
client is always an authenticated logged-in customer, so a 401 only fires
for callers that shouldn't be reaching the endpoint at all.

## Fix (server-only, split into two clean checks)
1. Explicit 401 at the door — before the DB fetch — with an honest
   'Authentication required' message.
2. Ownership check no longer needs the !userId branch — reads cleanly
   as "owner OR verified admin".

Both branches unchanged behaviorally for legitimate callers.

## Test
server/tests/reprice-401-hygiene.regression.test.ts — 3 pins:
  ✓ returns 401 explicitly when there is no userId
  ✓ 401 guard sits BEFORE the first db.select() (no wasted round-trip)
  ✓ ownership check no longer folds !userId into the 403 branch

    Test Files  1 passed (1)
         Tests  3 passed (3)

## Dependency
None. Completes the auth-slippage sweep on booking-requests.ts —
prior sweep PRs #1904 (confirm), #1911 (7 POSTs), #1912 (GET). This
covers the last remaining router-mounted handler with the same shape.

## Risk
Very low. 401 replaces 403 for anon callers only (a case that already
denied). Legitimate customer + admin repricing unchanged.

## Do not merge
Per standing CEO directive.

Merge pull request #7 from soundXlab/devin/1787069410-security-hardening

Security: fix auth bypasses, IDORs, path traversal, SSRF and permissive CORS

Security audit hardening: CORS, rate limiting, DTO validation, httpOnly session cookie, upload content-sniffing

Implements the fixes from this session's full security audit (Sections
5-8 plus remaining Section 3/4 items) that weren't already applied live:

- CORS: replace origin:'*' with an explicit allowlist (APP_URL/
  FRONTEND_URL/localhost) in the production Nest bootstrap
  (apps/web/src/lib/backendPort.ts). The previous config also paired
  wildcard origin with credentials:true, an invalid combination per the
  Fetch spec.

- Rate limiting: add @Throttle overrides on auth endpoints (login/
  register/verify/resend/forgot-password/reset-password) and on the two
  AI-generation endpoints, tighter than the app-wide default limiter.

- Server-side validation: convert ~13 inline @Body() object-literal types
  across auth/engine/media/oauth/posts controllers into real
  class-validator DTO classes, closing a gap where NestJS's global
  ValidationPipe silently validated nothing for non-class body types.

- Session storage: move the auth JWT from localStorage (readable by any
  XSS for up to 30 days) to an httpOnly cookie. AuthController.login sets
  it; a new AuthController.logout clears it. JwtStrategy reads it via a
  hand-rolled cookie parser (no new dependency). The frontend now caches
  only a non-sensitive user snapshot (id/email/name/brandId/expiry) for
  synchronous UI checks; apiFetch, the upload flow, the SSE stream, and
  the three OAuth connect links all rely on the cookie traveling
  automatically instead of a client-readable token.

- File upload content-sniffing: verify uploaded bytes actually match
  their claimed MIME type (magic-byte checks for JPEG/PNG/GIF/WEBP/
  ISOBMFF/EBML) on both the multer path and the direct-to-Blob register
  path, on top of the existing allowlist checks.

- OAuth error handling: stop reflecting err.message into redirect query
  params (info-disclosure risk); log full errors server-side, show
  generic messages to the user. Remove partial-secret and raw-code
  logging in the Instagram token exchange.

Also includes earlier uncommitted work from this session: the OAuth
state-signature CSRF bypass fix, IDOR fixes (createPost media ownership,
media folder parentId), MediaAsset atomic processing claim, TikTok
webhook signature verification, AI entitlement bypass fix, comment-
webhook dedup constraint, and unrelated UI/landing/billing changes.

Verified via full `tsc --noEmit` on apps/api (clean) and TypeScript
syntax-parsing across every edited frontend file; full-project `tsc` on
apps/web does not complete in this sandbox within a reasonable time, so
frontend changes are verified by syntax-parse + manual review rather than
a complete type-check. The JWT/httpOnly-cookie migration specifically has
not been exercised in a live browser this session -- recommend a manual
smoke test (login, logout, file upload, Instagram/TikTok/Drive connect)
before treating it as fully verified.

GHSA-pxmc-2ffp-8j67: prevent arbitrary certificate revocation via duplicate DB rows

Certificate identity was tracked only by Lemur's internal database row, not
by the actual CA-side certificate. Any authenticated user could upload a
duplicate record for a certificate they didn't own (matching an existing
authority_id and serial) and then revoke it, causing the CA to revoke the
real certificate belonging to another user.

- POST /api/1/certificates/upload now requires AuthorityPermission on the
  specified authority, and rejects uploads whose (authority_id, serial)
  pair already matches an existing certificate (409).
- PUT /api/1/certificates/<id>/revoke now checks authorization and endpoint
  attachment against every certificate row sharing (authority_id, serial)
  with the one being revoked, not just the row named in the request.

explanation:
The tile takes the artwork's own background (#177)

* admin: one-click suggested sell price from supplier cost

Enter the cost you pay (e.g. on Eldorado/Eneba) and get a 'Suggest price'
button that applies a ~18% markup with a €2 minimum profit, rounded to a
clean .99 — so €140 cost → €165.99, €10 → €11.99. Tune MARKUP/FLOOR in one
place. Existing margin readout stays.

* delivery: drop the Roblox-group join step from Robux (group is only for giveaways)

Robux delivery no longer mentions joining a Roblox group — the group is used
for giveaways, not delivery. Steps are now: enable 2FA → send your username →
we deliver. Updated on the site (EN/NL) and in the Discord bot.

* Forge Coins + Forge Shop, and 'as fast as possible' delivery label

- Forge Coins: a real loyalty currency (append-only ledger, balance = SUM,
  no cached number that can drift). Earn 1 coin per €10 of paid spend,
  awarded once per order (unique index = idempotent on payment retries).
- Forge Shop (account): spend coins on personal discount codes (€5/€10/€25,
  auto-generated single-use coupons) or a giveaway boost. Transactional
  redeem so concurrent spends can't overspend.
- API: GET /account/coins, POST /account/coins/redeem. Nav + route added.
- Migration 012_forge_coins.
- Product page: replaced the 'Estimated delivery ~Xs' line with a simple
  'Delivery: as fast as possible' (NL: 'Levering: zo snel mogelijk').

Verified on real Postgres: earn/idempotency/redeem/overspend all pass; build green.

* Mystery boxes — a real paid 'giveaway' (buy → roll a weighted prize → store credit)

- Migration 013: mystery_box_rewards (weighted prize pool) + mystery_pulls
  (what each buyer won). A mystery box is a product with kind='mystery'.
- mysteryBoxService: weighted roll per unit on payment, pays out as store
  credit via the wallet (tagged = idempotent, no double-pay on retries),
  records the pull + notifies the buyer.
- Hooked into order payment_received.
- Admin: 'Mystery box' toggle + a reward-pool editor (label / odds / € credit)
  in the product modal (GET+PUT /admin/products/:id/mystery).
- Product page: 'What's inside' panel showing every prize + REAL odds.
- Account order page: a celebratory reveal of what you won + credit added.
- Public GET /products/:id/mystery (pool+odds), account GET /orders/:id/mystery.

Verified on real Postgres: roll/credit/record + idempotent re-settle (6/6);
build green. Note: bundles already support any product mix (PS+Xbox, Apex+
Valorant) — create them in Admin → Monetization.

* i18n: Dutch labels for the mystery-box 'What's inside' panel

* Mystery boxes: bulk-luck ('more = better prizes') + a risk-free reroll (1x/box)

- Odds now scale with how many boxes are opened in one order: +8% luck per
  extra box (capped 2x), weighted toward the higher-value prizes — buy more,
  win better. Verified over a large sample (avg prize rises with quantity).
- One reroll per box (migration 014 stamps rerolled_at, claimed atomically so
  it can't be used twice): rolls a fresh prize and the buyer KEEPS the higher
  one — risk-free. POST /account/orders/:id/mystery/:pullId/reroll + a Reroll
  button on the order reveal.

Verified on real Postgres: reroll keeps-the-better + second reroll blocked; build green.

* Drop calendar — scheduled restocks/launches/sales

- Migration 015 + dropService: staff schedule drops (title, category, note,
  date/time); upcoming ones surface on the storefront.
- Public GET /api/drops (upcoming); admin GET/POST/DELETE /api/admin/drops.
- Storefront /drops page (timeline with 'Soon' badges, Discord-alert CTA)
  + a 'Drops' link in the top nav, fully bilingual.
- Admin: a 'Drops' tab in Monetization to schedule/remove drops.
- New drops announce to Discord (best-effort).

Verified on real Postgres (5/5: create/upcoming filter/list/delete); build green.

* Price history chart on product pages

- Migration 016 + price_history: a snapshot on product create and on every
  real price change (dup prices skipped); existing products get a baseline
  point so charts aren't empty.
- Public GET /api/products/:id/price-history.
- Product page: a clean SVG area/line chart with Now + Lowest, and a
  '🔥 lowest price ever' badge when current == lowest. Bilingual labels.

Verified on real Postgres (baseline + change tracking + dedup, 3/3); build green.

* Launch polish: surface engagement features + Discord /drops

Site: a 'Save more & win big' section on the homepage with cards linking to
Forge Coins, Mystery boxes and the Drop calendar — so the new features are
actually discoverable (bilingual).

Discord: new /drops command showing the upcoming drop calendar (live from the
store, with Discord relative timestamps) + a link to the full calendar;
registered and added to /help.

* Live trust stats: refresh instantly on delivery + new review (no fabrication)

The trust stats (delivered count, customers, review count, average rating) are
already computed 100% from real DB rows — nothing seeded or padded (demoSeed
only inserts products; no hardcoded numbers in the UI). This makes them update
INSTANTLY instead of within the 15s cache window: bust the social/stats cache
the moment an order is marked delivered and the moment a review is added, so
the counters and average rating move up right away.

Verified on real Postgres: delivered increments on completion, review count +
rating reflect a real review; boots with no circular-import issue.

* Launch-ready hardening: zero-admin setup, critical fixes, self-running maintenance

Critical fixes:
- productSchema rejected kind='mystery' (enum was digital|physical) → the
  admin's Mystery box toggle could never save. Added 'mystery'.
- Admin fulfillment badge counted status='paid', which doesn't exist →
  always 0. Now counts payment_received/processing/awaiting_fulfillment.

Zero-admin launch:
- Self-scheduling maintenance: piggybacks on live traffic (max 1×/hour per
  instance, non-blocking) so OTP purges, stale-order cleanup and payment
  reminders run WITHOUT CRON_SECRET or Vercel Cron. Launch-check item is
  now ok by default (cron stays as optional backup).
- Starter content on first boot (idempotent, never overwrites admin work):
  the €49.99 Forge Mystery Box with a balanced 5-prize pool (EV ≈ €38.75 →
  ~22% margin, paid as store credit) + an FPS Duo bundle (Apex+Valorant,
  10% off). 'mystery' category gets its own card visual.

Quality:
- Mystery-only orders now AUTO-COMPLETE on payment (the credit payout IS
  the delivery) instead of lingering in the manual queue.
- Forge Shop: redeemed coupon codes persist in the coin history with a
  copy button (a toast was the only place you ever saw the code).

Verified on real Postgres: 5/5 hardening e2e (maintenance fires on traffic,
launch-check ok without CRON_SECRET, mystery auto-complete, fulfillment
query, code-in-history) + 4/4 starter-content e2e + 19/19 regression suite;
build green.

* Discord relay: full automation with ZERO hosting-side Discord secrets + badge fix

The 'Discord automation' launch warning could only be cleared by putting the
bot token / webhook URLs into Vercel. Now the community bot (which already has
the token) pulls the store's events itself:

- Migration 017: discord_outbox queue + a tiny kv table.
- discordService: every sender (order pings, drops, stock alerts, 500 alerts)
  posts directly when a webhook is configured, and otherwise QUEUES the exact
  embed payload in the outbox. Delivery DMs relay the same way (channel 'dm'
  with the buyer's linked Discord id) when no server-side bot token exists.
- POST /api/discord/outbox — HMAC-signed like the digest; returns + marks
  pending events, stamps 'bot seen' in kv, prunes old rows.
- Bot: polls the outbox every 60s and posts events to #leads / #deals (with
  fallbacks) or DMs the buyer. Zero new env vars — reuses REVIEW_INGEST_SECRET.
- Launch check: 'Discord automation' turns OK as soon as the bot has polled in
  the last 24h ('Bot connected via relay'), with a clear hint otherwise.

Also: the admin Support badge now counts only OPEN tickets (action needed), so
resolving a ticket clears the badge — 'pending' means waiting on the customer.

Verified on real Postgres over real HTTP: queue → signed poll → delivered →
second poll empty → bad signature 403 → launch check flips to ok (8/8);
bot load test + build green.

* bot: watchdog retries before paging (cold start / Neon wake is not an outage)

The site watchdog alerted @here after a single failed 15s probe — but a
serverless cold start plus a sleeping Neon database can take 15-25s to wake,
which is a false alarm, not downtime. Verified the API itself is healthy: a
cold boot from a COMPLETELY fresh database (all 17 migrations + seeds) answers
/api/health in ~1.3s, warm in ~12ms. Now the watchdog retries once after 20s
with a 28s timeout and only pages when both probes fail — real outages still
alert within ~1 minute.

* Fix everything reported live + product art + email v3

Fixes from live testing:
- Duplicate €49.99 mystery boxes: the starter seeder raced when Vercel booted
  several instances at once. Now uses a FIXED primary key (insert ON CONFLICT
  DO NOTHING) and heals existing duplicates on boot (keeps the oldest; deletes
  or deactivates extras). Verified with 3 parallel seed calls → exactly 1 box.
- 'Fortnite Accounts' removed from the home sidebar — it was a hardcoded entry
  pointing at the v-bucks category; we don't sell accounts.
- 'Happy customers' now counts people who actually WROTE A REVIEW (stat tile +
  hero avatar row), not everyone who ever ordered — and hides at zero.
- Orders badge vs Fulfillment badge: Orders now shows paid orders awaiting
  delivery; Fulfillment counts exactly the manual queue its page displays.
- Forge Coins grant bug: the order-earn dedupe index blocked a second grant by
  the same admin (same reason+ref) — grants now store ref NULL (attribution is
  in the audit log).

New:
- Write a review on /reviews: verified buyers pick one of their delivered
  orders (new GET /account/reviewable), star + text → posts via the existing
  verified-review endpoint. Guests see how reviews work. Bilingual.
- Admin → Users: 🪙 Coins button to give (or deduct) Forge Coins per user
  (POST /admin/security/users/:id/coins, audited, can't go below 0).
- Product art: per-pack denomination cards (the existing pack SVGs) now win
  over the generic category icon, and syncCatalogImages() backfills them on
  every boot so the LIVE catalog gets its art too.
- Email v3: richer shell for ALL mails (patterned gradient header, badge,
  pill styles) + a redesigned login-code email (lock badge, expiry pill).
  Previous body registered as legacy so deployed DBs auto-upgrade.

Proven on real Postgres (8/8): parallel-seed dedupe, duplicate healing, double
grant, over-deduct block, redeemed code REALLY gives €10 off €25 at checkout,
single-use enforced, reviewable query, queue count. Build green.

* starter: heal duplicate bundles (6x FPS Duo Pack from the pre-fix race)

The old bundle seeder created a random-id bundle per concurrent cold start
before the fixed-id fix shipped, leaving 6 identical 'FPS Duo Pack' rows in
production. Boot now dedupes same-named bundles (keeps the oldest, tiebreak
on id for same-instant rows; bundles have no dependents so DELETE is safe).

Reproduced exactly (6 identical rows, 3 sharing one timestamp) → heals to 1;
parallel re-runs stay at 1 (3/3 on real Postgres).

* Audit round: reroll safety, phone-route crash fix, /balance Discord command

- rerollPull: validate the pull + a non-empty reward pool BEFORE atomically
  claiming the one-time reroll, so an emptied pool can no longer burn the
  buyer's free reroll and crash the request.
- account routes: import badRequest (phone verify routes threw a 500
  ReferenceError on any invalid input instead of a clean 400).
- New signed endpoint POST /api/discord/balance: Forge Coins, store credit
  and loyalty tier for a linked Discord member; the uid is bound into the
  HMAC signature so requests can't be replayed for another member.
- Bot: new /balance command (ephemeral) + /help entry; unlinked members get
  a login pointer.

Verified on real Postgres: 23-check purchase-flow e2e (createOrder ->
payment -> mystery settle -> coins -> auto-complete -> reroll paths),
7-check balance-endpoint HTTP e2e, 19-check regression suite, bot load
test, vite build.

* Add /clearpins staff command to bulk-delete "pinned a message" notices

Every time something is pinned, Discord posts a small "X pinned a message to
this channel" system message. Our setup panels pin on boot, so these pile up.

/clearpins (staff-only) walks the history of every text + announcement channel
and deletes just those pin-notice system messages (MessageType 6) in one go —
normal messages and other system notices are left untouched. Deletes
individually so notices older than 14 days are handled too, paginating up to a
safety cap per channel. Optional `here:true` limits it to the current channel.
Reports how many were removed and calls out any channels it lacked
Manage Messages / Read Message History for.

Verified with a mocked-interaction test: only pin notices deleted across text +
announcement channels, voice channels not scanned, unmanageable channels
skipped and reported; bot load test + lint still green.

* Document REVIEW_INGEST_SECRET in the bot .env.example

The bot needs REVIEW_INGEST_SECRET to poll the signed store relay (order
pings, drops, delivery DMs) and to read /balance and /digest, but it was
missing from the example env file — easy to forget when deploying to a host.
Add it with a note that it must match the value in Vercel, and point the

* Fix 5 bugs found in a full site + Discord audit

Frontend
- Checkout page crashed on render: the main component called t() dozens of
  times but never ran useI18n() (only the helper sub-components did), so the
  whole checkout threw a ReferenceError the moment the cart had items. Nobody
  could reach the pay step. Added const { t } = useI18n().

Server
- Gift-card codes were derived purely from Date.now() mod 32, so only 32
  distinct codes could ever be generated — trivially guessable/enumerable
  (drain any outstanding card via the public balance check + redeem) and
  colliding on the UNIQUE index after a few issues. Now generated with
  crypto.randomInt over a 32-char alphabet (~10^24 space); proven 20000/20000
  unique.
- Manual-payment proof confirm/reject never notified the buyer: it checked
  order.user_id, but getOrder() hydrates to camelCase order.userId, so the
  guard was always false. Fixed both call sites; the reject email's order link
  was also an empty string — now points at the public track page.

Discord bot
- Auto-moderation + XP ran inside CLAIMED tickets: claiming renames the
  channel to '✋-ticket-…', which defeated the startsWith('ticket-') check, so
  a customer pasting a trade link in their own claimed ticket got their
  message deleted and publicly warned. Detect tickets by their stable
  'ticket-owner:' topic (survives the rename) via a shared isTicketChannel().
- /suggest could report 'interaction failed' while actually posting: it did
  two Discord round-trips (send + startThread) before its first reply, risking
  the 3s ACK window. Now defers first, then edits the reply.

Verified on real Postgres + mocked-bot: new bugfix e2e (7 checks: proof
confirm/reject notifications, gift-card uniqueness/shape), ticket-exemption
test (scam in a claimed ticket is left alone, public channel still moderated),
gift-card entropy (20000/20000 unique), plus the full suite green — flow-e2e
(23), regression (19), bot load test, and vite build.

* Fix slow first request (cold start): defer non-critical boot work

Symptom: signup / 'send code' could take ~15s. Cause: ensureReady() — which the
serverless handler awaits before EVERY request on a cold instance — ran heavy
upkeep synchronously on each boot: ~11 email-template queries, per-product art
backfill across the whole catalog (~70+ products), and starter-content dedupe.
On a cold Neon connection those ~100 sequential round-trips stacked up before
the request (and its OTP email) even started.

Now ensureReady only awaits what a request truly needs — migrate (schema),
seed on an empty DB, and stocking an empty catalog — and defers the rest
(syncEmailTemplates upgrade, seedStarterContent, syncCatalogImages) to a
one-shot background task that runs after we're ready to serve.

Measured locally: on an already-seeded DB the blocking boot dropped from doing
~100 queries to 3 (~36ms); on cold Neon that removes the multi-second stall.
The empty-DB path is unchanged (seed() still installs roles/permissions/all
templates synchronously, so auth + OTP work on the very first request).

Verified: boot e2e (6 checks — roles, catalog and login_otp template ready
immediately; 2nd ensureReady memoised; starter box + bundle appear via
background upkeep). Regression (19), lint, build green.

* Supplier listing URLs + serial one-order-at-a-time fulfillment queue

Extends supplier auto-fulfillment so the owner can paste a listing link (e.g. an

- Migration 021: supplier_products.supplier_url. mapSupplierProduct stores it,
  the admin mapping route + Suppliers.jsx get a 'Listing URL' field, and the
  mapping list shows/links it. The URL is passed into the connector's
  createFulfillment (EldoradoConnector forwards it as listingUrl).
- Serial queue (fulfillmentService): on payment, instead of firing a per-order
  fulfillment, we drain a queue that processes paid supplier orders ONE AT A
  TIME, oldest first — finishing (buy + deliver) one before starting the next.
  A short DB lease (kv row + TTL) guarantees only one worker drains at a time
  across serverless instances; an 'attempted' set advances past orders that open
  no request (margin-guarded) instead of looping; async in-progress buys are
  re-polled from maintenance. Also drained from maintenance as a safety net.

Reality note kept honest in the UI copy: a bare marketplace link can only be
auto-purchased when the connector has a real buy API (Eldorado apiKey); the
queue + link plumbing makes it fully automatic the moment that's configured.

Verified on real Postgres: serial-queue e2e (8 checks — URL stored + passed to

completed, a second drain skips under the lease, no double-buying) and the

stalls the queue). Regression (19), lint, build green.

* Audit round: fix payment, coin, and supplier auto-buy money/security bugs

Full audit of the manual-payments, supplier auto-buy, Forge+/coins/wallet,
trust-stats, cold-start and security surfaces. Stats, cold-start, DB
parameterization, admin authz and secret handling verified solid; the
confirmed defects below are fixed and covered by e2e tests.

Payments
- orderService: make the order status transition atomic (conditional UPDATE
  guarded on the observed status + change check). Concurrent confirms / a
  webhook racing a manual confirm can no longer dispense, email or complete an
  order twice.
- paymentProofService: atomically claim a proof (UPDATE ... WHERE status=
  'pending') so a double-click / second admin can't drive a second
  markPaymentReceived; reject non-http(s) screenshot links (zod .url() also
  passes javascript:/data:, a stored-XSS vector in the admin queue); flag the
  2nd proof as multiple_submissions (was off-by-one at the 3rd).
- catalog: reject the screenshot URL at the route too; disable the demo
  self-pay route whenever a real payment method is configured.
- Checkout: show the server order total on the pay-instructions screen — the
  cart is cleared first, so the old cart-derived amount read €0.00.

Forge Coins / membership
- forgeCoinService: lock the user row (FOR UPDATE) before summing in
  spendCoins/redeemReward/grantCoins, matching walletService. Concurrent
  spends can no longer both pass the balance check (negative balance / free
  rewards / free membership).
- account: charge + grant membership in one transaction (no "charged without
  membership", no partial grant).

Supplier auto-buy
- Kinguin/Eldorado: never mark an order fulfilled with zero delivered keys —
  a transient error fetching the keys kept the order in_progress to re-poll
  instead of completing it empty-handed (paid supplier, buyer got nothing).
- fulfillment margin guard: treat an unknown (null) supplier cost as
  do-not-auto-buy, and compare cost to the buyer's effective post-discount
  revenue per unit instead of list price (no blind uncapped buys, no buying at
  a loss on discounted orders).
- G2A: fix the doubled /v3 path prefix (every call 404'd), pass order
  quantity with a line-level max_price cap, and collect multiple keys.
